title: RIL Q1FY27 Results: Revenue tops Rs 3 lakh crore, retail hits 396 million users - 5 key highlights
snippet: Jul 17, 2026 · Reliance Industries reported strong Q1 FY27 results with double-digit growth in telecom, retail, and oil-to-chemicals, driven by Jio and retail businesses amid steady new energy investments.
content:
Reliance Industries started FY27 on a strong note supported by strong performance in its telecom, retail and oil-to-chemicals (O2C) businesses. All the three verticals delivered double-digit growth. Consumer businesses, led by Jio and Retail, contributed more than half of Reliance’s consolidated EBITDA during the quarter.
Commenting on the performance, Reliance Industries Chairman and Managing Director Mukesh Ambani said the company has made a steady start to FY27 despite geopolitical tensions and volatile commodity markets.
The Mukesh Ambani-led conglomerate reported a 24.5% year-on-year (YoY) rise in consolidated revenue to Rs 3.40 lakh crore in the June quarter. EBITDA rose 10.1% YoY to a record Rs 54,067 crore.
Here are 5 key highlights from Reliance Industries’ Q1FY27 performance
1. Jio Platforms Q1 profit rises 9.2%
Jio Platforms reported a 9.2%increase in profit after tax to Rs 7,764 crore. The growth was driven by sustained gains in subscriber market share, ARPU and sale of digital services.
Jio Platforms (JPL), the digital and telecom arm of Reliance Industries, posted revenue at Rs from operations at Rs 39,173 crore, increasing by 11.8% year-on-year (YoY).
“The Digital Services business continued its growth momentum during the quarter. Jio’s performance across mobility, home broadband and enterprise services remained strong, driving healthy earnings growth of 15% YoY,” Reliance Industries Chairman and Managing Director, Mukesh Ambani said in a statement.
During the quarter, Jio Platforms filed its DRHP with Sebi, which is a significant step towards its public listing, he added.
“The upcoming IPO will be an important milestone in Jio’s journey and will give investors an opportunity to participate in India’s digital growth story,” Ambani said.
Jio’s average revenue per user (ARPU) increased by 3.3% to Rs 215.6 from Rs 208.8 a year ago on a better subscriber mix and positive seasonality, partly impacted by promotional schemes for fixed broadband customers.
Its customer base increased by 7.1% YoY to 53.3 crore from 49.8 crore in the June 2026 quarter.
2. Reliance Retail crosses 396 million customers; Digital grocery orders jump 116%
Reliance Retail reported gross revenue of Rs 90,408 crore, up 7.4% YoY.
Excluding the impact of the consumer brands business restructuring, revenue grew 11.6% YoY.
The retailer’s registered customer base increased to 396 million, while quarterly transactions jumped 46% YoY to 568 million.
Reliance Retail now operates 20,169 stores across more than 7,000 towns. Grocery orders through digital platforms surged 116% YoY during the quarter.
However, EBITDA declined 1.1% YoY to Rs 6,309 crore, while profit after tax fell 14.1% YoY to Rs 2,805 crore due to continued investments in digital commerce and hyperlocal delivery.
The company said these investments are expected to support long-term growth, with a target to double operating EBITDA over the next three years.
3. O2C business clocks strong growth supported by higher refining margins
Reliance’s oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business reported a strong quarter, supported by higher refining and petrochemical margins.
Revenue increased 30.4% YoY to Rs 2.02 lakh crore, while EBITDA rose 17.2% YoY to Rs 17,010 crore, the highest in four years.
The company benefited from stronger fuel cracks, improved downstream margins and the cost advantage of ethane cracking. It also diversified crude sourcing from Russia and Latin America and redirected exports to higher-margin international markets.
However, profitability was partly impacted by domestic fuel retail under-recoveries, windfall tax-related costs and planned refinery maintenance.
4. Oil and gas business remains steady
Reliance’s oil and gas segment reported revenue of Rs 6,298 crore, up 3.2% YoY.
EBITDA remained largely stable at Rs 4,973 crore despite lower KG-D6 gas production and prices.
Higher crude oil prices and improved coal-bed methane (CBM) production helped offset the decline in gas volumes.
5. Reliance Industries spends Rs 38,682 crore on future growth
Capital expenditure for the quarter stood at Rs 38,682 crore, with the company citing continued investment in O2C expansion and new energy projects, alongside its consumer business infrastructure. Net debt stood at Rs 1,22,914 crore, with net debt-to-EBITDA at a conservative 0.57 times.
Conclusion
Reliance Industries said it continues to accelerate work on its new energy business.
The company plans to begin installation work at its Kutch renewable energy project after the monsoon. It aims to scale up installation to 55 MWp of solar capacity and 150 MWh of batteries every day by next year.
“I remain confident in the underlying strength of our businesses and in the talent and commitment of our people. The start to FY27 gives me reason to be optimistic about the year ahead as we move forward with phased commissioning of new energy projects and unlock value through the Jio IPO,” he added.

title: Reliance Industries Q4 results key takeaways: O2C drags profit down 12.6% as Jio, retail hold the fort
snippet: Apr 24, 2026 · Reliance Industries Limited saw its net profit fall 12.6 percent in the March quarter. This was due to challenges in its oil-to-chemicals segment. However, its consumer businesses like Jio Platforms and Reliance Retail performed well. For the full year, Reliance achieved record profits and revenue.
content:
The company's consumer-facing businesses, however, continued to scale, with Jio Platforms posting strong earnings growth and Reliance Retail crossing 20,000 stores.
Also Read: RIL announces Q4 results today. 5 things to watch out for investors reeling under stock crash
Consolidated net profit attributable to owners of the company came in at Rs 16,971 crore for Q4FY26, down from Rs 19,407 crore in the same quarter last year. Gross revenue rose 12.9% year-on-year to Rs 3,25,290 crore.
For the full year FY26, consolidated PAT rose 18.3% to a record Rs 95,610 crore, with gross revenue hitting a record Rs 11,75,919 crore, up 9.8% year-on-year.
Commenting on the results, Chairman and Managing Director Mukesh Ambani said, "Through fiscal FY2025-26 we faced geopolitical disruptions, volatile energy prices and shifting global trade patterns.
These headwinds weighed on businesses across the world. India held its economic growth course through all this, as did Reliance. The breadth of our portfolio and strong domestic orientation helped navigate volatility in the external environment."
The board recommended a dividend of Rs 6 per share for FY26.
Here are 10 key takeaways from the Q4FY26 results:
1. Quarterly profit fell 12.6% YoY: Full-year PAT at a record Consolidated net profit attributable to owners stood at Rs 16,971 crore in Q4FY26, down from Rs 19,407 crore in Q4FY25 and Rs 18,645 crore in Q3FY26. On a full-year basis, however, consolidated PAT rose 18.3% year-on-year to a record Rs 95,610 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 80,787 crore in FY25.
2. Revenue hit a record for the full year: Gross revenue for Q4FY26 rose 12.9% year-on-year to Rs 3,25,290 crore. For the full year, consolidated gross revenue rose 9.8% to a record Rs 11,75,919 crore. Full-year EBITDA also hit a record at Rs 2,07,911 crore, up 13.4% year-on-year.
3. O2C remained the key drag in the quarter: The oil-to-chemicals segment reported quarterly EBITDA of Rs 14,520 crore in Q4FY26, down 3.7% from Rs 15,080 crore in Q4FY25. A sharp rise in crude premiums on physical barrels, elevated freight and insurance costs, weak polymer deltas, and under-recoveries at Jio-bp fuel retail outlets weighed on earnings.
The reintroduction of the Special Additional Excise Duty on diesel and ATF exports also impacted the segment. RIL diverted propane and butane to boost LPG output and KGD6 gas to priority sectors during the quarter in response to disruptions caused by the Strait of Hormuz closure.
4. Jio Platforms was the standout performer: Jio Platforms reported quarterly EBITDA of Rs 20,060 crore in Q4FY26, up 17.9% from Rs 17,016 crore in Q4FY25, with EBITDA margin expanding 230 basis points to 52.4%.
For the full year, Jio EBITDA rose to Rs 76,255 crore from Rs 64,170 crore in FY25. Total subscriber base stood at 524.4 million as of March 2026, including 268 million 5G subscribers. ARPU for the quarter came in at Rs 214 per subscriber per month, up from Rs 206.2 a year ago. Data traffic grew 35% year-on-year to 66 exabytes in Q4FY26.
Also Read: Reliance Industries to declare dividend this week: Here's how Mukesh Ambani-led company rewarded its 42 lakh shareholders so far
5. Reliance Retail crossed 20,000 stores: Reliance Retail Ventures posted quarterly EBITDA of Rs 6,921 crore in Q4FY26, up 3.1% from Rs 6,711 crore in Q4FY25. For the full year, retail revenue rose 11.8% to Rs 3,70,026 crore and EBITDA grew 7.9% to Rs 27,033 crore. The total store count crossed 20,000, reaching 20,160 stores as of March 2026.
The registered customer base stood at 387 million, with 1.93 billion annual transactions recorded during FY26. Hyper-local daily orders were up over 300% year-on-year in Q4.
6. Oil and gas EBITDA fell sharply in the quarter: The upstream oil and gas segment reported quarterly EBITDA of Rs 4,195 crore in Q4FY26, down 18.1% from Rs 5,123 crore in Q4FY25. The decline was on account of lower gas price realisation in KGD6 and CBM fields, lower KGD6 gas volumes, and higher operating costs due to maintenance activity and government levies. The average KGD6 gas price realised in Q4FY26 was $9.63/MMBTU versus $10.09/MMBTU in Q4FY25.
7. Full-year EBITDA hit a record across segments: Total consolidated EBITDA for FY26 rose 13.4% year-on-year to a record Rs 2,07,911 crore. Jio Platforms EBITDA grew 18.8% for the full year, retail EBITDA grew 7.9%, and O2C EBITDA grew 10.1% on a full-year basis, even as quarterly O2C performance remained under pressure due to geopolitical headwinds and elevated input costs.
8. JioStar emerged as a new earnings contributor: The JioStar business reported quarterly revenue of Rs 9,784 crore and EBITDA of Rs 827 crore for Q4FY26. JioHotstar averaged 500 million monthly active users during the quarter. The T20 Men's Cricket World Cup Final achieved a peak concurrency of 72.5 million, a global record. For the full year FY26, JioStar posted revenue of Rs 36,248 crore and EBITDA of Rs 4,885 crore.
9. Jio Platforms listing on the horizon: Mukesh Ambani, in his commentary on the results, said the company is advancing steadily towards the listing of Jio Platforms, describing it as a defining milestone in Jio's journey. He also noted that Reliance is making rapid progress in operationalising its New Energy giga-factories, which he said will emerge as a powerful growth engine for the company and a transformative contributor to India's energy future.
10. Board recommends Rs 6 dividend; cash position strengthened: The board of directors recommended a dividend of Rs 6 per fully paid-up equity share of Rs 10 each for FY26, subject to shareholder approval at the annual general meeting.
Cash and cash equivalents as of March 31, 2026 stood at Rs 2,49,704 crore, up from Rs 2,30,447 crore a year earlier. Capital expenditure for Q4FY26 stood at Rs 40,560 crore, taking full-year capex to Rs 1,44,271 crore.

title: Reliance Q2 FY27 Results on Oct 30: Rs 20,900 Crore Profit
snippet: Oct 28, 2026 · Reliance Industries Limited (RIL), led by Mukesh Ambani, is scheduled to announce its September-quarter results on Friday, October 30, 2026. Investors will be watching closely to see whether stronger refining margins and telecom growth can offset weaker performance in some business segments.
content:
Reliance Q2 FY27 Results on Oct 30: Rs 20,900 Crore Profit Seen, Retail the Weak Link
Reliance Industries Limited (RIL), led by Mukesh Ambani, is scheduled to announce its September-quarter results on Friday, October 30, 2026. Investors will be watching closely to see whether stronger refining margins and telecom growth can offset weaker performance in some business segments.
According to the company’s regulatory filing dated October 27, the board will consider the standalone and consolidated unaudited financial results for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026.
Reliance has not specified the exact time of the announcement. An analyst meeting is scheduled to follow the board meeting, providing an opportunity to discuss financial performance and business updates.
The board will also consider raising funds through non-convertible debentures (NCDs) on a private-placement basis, potentially in one or more tranches.
Track Live : Nifty Levels Today | Sensex Levels Today
Why Analysts Expect Stronger Reliance Q2 FY27 Results Earnings
Brokerage estimates point to improved profitability, supported primarily by the oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business.
Nuvama Research expects consolidated EBITDA to increase 17% year-on-year to ₹53,700 crore, while profit after tax (PAT) is projected to rise 15% to ₹20,900 crore.
Kotak Institutional Equities has also projected consolidated EBITDA growth of around 15% year-on-year and 11.1% quarter-on-quarter.
These figures are forecasts, not confirmed results. The actual performance will depend on refining margins, production volumes, operating costs and the contribution of individual business segments.
Official results date, board agenda and analyst meeting
Reliance Industries confirmed in its October 27 regulatory filing that its board would meet on Friday, October 30, 2026, to consider the unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026. The board will also consider raising funds through non-convertible debentures (NCDs) via private placement. An analyst meeting will follow the board meeting.
| Key detail | Information | 
|---|---|
| Results date | Friday, October 30, 2026 | 
| Reporting period | Q2 FY27 and first half of FY27 | 
| Exact results announcement time | Not specified in the cited filing | 
| Analyst meeting | After the board meeting | 
| Fundraising proposal | Listed, secured or unsecured, redeemable NCDs | 
| Proposed fundraising amount | Not specified in the cited filing | 
| Dividend announcement | No dividend proposal identified in the cited board-meeting notice | 
Nuvama’s Q2 FY27 earnings estimates
Nuvama Research expects Reliance Industries to report stronger earnings, primarily driven by its oil-to-chemicals business and improved refining margins.
| Financial indicator | Nuvama estimate | Expected performance | 
|---|---|---|
| Consolidated revenue | ₹2,92,437 crore | Up 14.9% YoY | 
| Consolidated EBITDA | ₹53,700 crore | Up 17% YoY | 
| Profit after tax (PAT) | ₹20,905–20,900 crore | Up approximately 15% YoY | 
| O2C EBITDA | ₹20,700 crore | Up 38% YoY | 
| Digital services EBITDA | Not specified in the cited report | Expected to benefit from ARPU growth and subscriber additions | 
| Reliance Retail EBITDA | Not specified in the cited report | Expected to remain relatively weak | 
| Oil and gas EBITDA | Not specified in the cited report | Expected to face pressure from lower production and gas realisations | 
How the O2C Business Could Drive Reliance Industries’ Performance
Reliance’s O2C business is expected to be a major earnings driver during Q2 FY27.
Nuvama estimates that O2C EBITDA could rise 38% year-on-year to ₹20,700 crore. Improved refining margins, higher refinery throughput, stronger gasoil and aviation turbine fuel cracks, better gasoline cracks and inventory gains could support the segment.
Other brokerage estimates suggest an even sharper year-on-year improvement, highlighting the importance of refining performance to the overall earnings outlook.
Investors will also monitor the impact of the rupee’s weakness and the company’s petrochemical operations. However, fluctuations in global commodity prices and refining margins could affect the final numbers.
What Jio Platforms and Reliance Retail Could Contribute
Jio Platforms is expected to maintain growth through subscriber additions and average revenue per user (ARPU) improvements. Its digital services business has delivered strong growth in recent quarters, making telecom performance an important part of the RIL earnings outlook.
The results follow Jio Platforms’ ₹30,213 crore IPO, which closed on October 23, with its shares scheduled to list on October 28, 2026. Jio Platforms is also scheduled to announce its earnings on October 30.

title: Inflation (PCE)
snippet: Aug 2, 2024 · Keeping inflation low and stable is one of the Federal Reserve's goals when conducting monetary policy. How does the inflation rate factor into the Fed's policy decisions? The Federal Reserve has a dual mandate to promote maximum employment and stable prices for the American people.
content:
Economy at a Glance - Inflation (PCE)
What is inflation?
Inflation is the rate at which the price of goods and services increases over time. Keeping inflation low and stable is one of the Federal Reserve's goals when conducting monetary policy.
How does the inflation rate factor into the Fed's policy decisions?
The Federal Reserve has a dual mandate to promote maximum employment and stable prices for the American people. Federal Reserve policymakers closely monitor the rate of inflation and adjust monetary policy to help steer the inflation rate toward its target while also continuing to promote the goal of maximum employment.
What is the Fed's inflation target?
The Federal Reserve seeks to achieve inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures (PCE).
Why does the Fed target PCE inflation instead of the CPI?
To measure inflation across the entire economy, economists produce price indexes to see how overall prices for goods and services are changing. Two common price indexes are the consumer price index (CPI) and the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index. While the two are similar, the PCE index is constructed in a way that accounts for how Americans are spending their money at a given time and more quickly adapts to changes in spending patterns.

title: Economy at a Glance - Policy Rate
snippet: Jun 19, 2014 · Changes in the target range for the federal funds rate influence short-term interest rates for other financial instruments, which in turn affect the spending decisions of households and businesses and thus have implications for economic activity, employment, and inflation.
content:
Economy at a Glance - Policy Rate
Note: The effective dates for federal funds rate target range changes correspond to the day after the conclusion of the meeting.
What is the federal funds rate?
The federal funds rate is the interest rate charged by banks to borrow from each other overnight. The Federal Reserve influences this rate through monetary policy decisions.
Who sets the target range for the federal funds rate?
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets a target range for the federal funds rate. The FOMC has eight regularly scheduled meetings each year and announces its policy decisions at 2 p.m. Eastern Time on the second day of each meeting. The FOMC is made up of members of the Board of Governors, who are based in Washington, D.C., and Federal Reserve Bank presidents from around the country.
How do changes in the target range for the federal funds rate affect the economy?
Changes in the target range for the federal funds rate influence short-term interest rates for other financial instruments, which in turn affect the spending decisions of households and businesses and thus have implications for economic activity, employment, and inflation.
How does the Federal Reserve keep the federal funds rate in the target range?
The Federal Reserve steers the federal funds rate into its target range primarily by changing the interest rate paid on reserve balances and the interest rate of its overnight reverse repurchase facility. Changes in these rates influence the borrowing activity of banks and other financial institutions.

title: Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time since 2023
snippet: Sep 17, 2026 · The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023 on Wednesday, reversing course as the Iran war drives up global energy prices and fuels inflation.
content:
Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time since 2023
The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023 on Wednesday, reversing course as the Iran war drives up global energy prices and fuels inflation.
The Fed raised the federal funds rate by 0.25 percentage points, bringing its target range to between 3.75% and 4% — its highest level since December 2025. The benchmark rate influences borrowing costs across the U.S. economy, including for credit cards, auto loans and personal loans.
In a set of quarterly projections, the Fed also signaled that its rate-setting committee expects to further raise rates later this year. The vote to hike rates was unanimous, the Fed said in a statement on Wednesday.
No rate hikes in 2027
For now, however, the Fed's move doesn't appear to signal the start of an aggressive rate-hiking campaign. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday that policymakers expect to hold rates steady throughout 2027.
"For more than five years, inflation has been running above target," Warsh said at a news conference after the rate announcement. "So our predominant focus is on the price stability side of our mandate. The plain fact is that inflation is too high, and has been for too long."
About half of FOMC members predicted that rates would hold steady next year.
"We don't think this is the beginning of another major tightening cycle, and markets have too much tightening priced in over the coming year," Michael Pearce, chief U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, said in a research note.
By contrast, the central bank raised rates 11 times starting in 2022 as it sought to quash surging inflation as the economy was rebounding from the pandemic.
Still, the latest hike marks an about-face from the Fed's stance at the start of the year, when inflation was cooling, and as many economists expected the central bank to lower interest rates throughout 2026. Instead, monetary policymakers are brandishing their most potent weapon to curb prices. The Consumer Price Index rose at an annual rate of 3.4% in August, far above the Fed's 2% annual target.
President Trump has repeatedly called on the Fed to lower borrowing costs. But escalating conflict in the Middle East has disrupted crude oil production and supplies, pushing up fuel prices in the U.S. and driving up costs across the broader economy.
When asked on Wednesday how the president might react to the rate increase, Warsh said, "I've got nothing for you on a discussion with the president."
In a Truth Social post on Wednesday after the Fed policy statement, Mr. Trump said U.S. interest rates "should be 1%, or less, because we are the Best Credit in the World — BY FAR."
"LOWER THE INTEREST RATES FOR THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, AND FAST!" he added.
Why stocks fell after Warsh comments
"Hiking was the right move, and it restores Fed credibility that the central bank will curb inflation no matter what the White House or anyone else says," Heather Long, chief economist at the Navy Federal Credit Union, said in an email. "The big news is that the vote was unanimous and the forecast only signals one more hike in 2026."
Higher interest rates can tamp down inflation because consumers pare spending and businesses reduce investment. That cools economic growth and tempers price increases as demand slows.
Stocks tumbled after Warsh said the U.S. economy "appears to be strengthening" and reiterated his pledge to tame inflation. Some investors interpreted his remarks as a sign that the central bank believes the economy can withstand additional rate hikes if they are needed to finally get inflation under control.
"Stocks declined after Warsh finished. Why? Warsh was hawkish today," Long said. "How many more hikes beyond that remains an open question that likely will depend on the war in Iran and just how insatiable the data center building boom is."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 631 points, or 1.2%, to close at 51,462, while the S&P 500 lost almost 0.4%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq ended the day largely flat.
Higher borrowing costs
Banks are likely to respond to the latest Fed hike by boosting their interest rates on credit cards and other lending products, although a single 0.25 percentage-point increase might not significantly raise borrowing costs, according to financial experts.
Even so, the increase in borrowing costs comes as Americans are shouldering higher costs for gas, food and other essentials.
"Consumer sentiment is now 13% below where it was this time last year," said Heather Boushey, professor of practice at the Kleinman Center for Energy Policy at the University of Pennsylvania, in an email. The Fed's rate hike this week "will make it harder for families to borrow, raising the cost of car loans, credit cards, mortgages and more."

title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains high
snippet: Oct 29, 2026 · The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday after hiking borrowing costs in September to clamp down on inflation. The central bank left the federal funds rate at a target range of ...
content:
Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains high
The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday after hiking borrowing costs in September to clamp down on inflation.
The central bank left the federal funds rate at a target range of 3.75% to 4%, keeping it unchanged after raising rates last month for the first time in three years.
In a statement, the Fed said economic activity is growing at a "strong pace" while acknowledging that inflation remains elevated.
"The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2% goal," Fed officials said.
Wall Street had forecast that the Fed would stand pat on rates. Investor reaction was muted, with the three major indexes remaining essentially flat after the Fed's announcement.
The Fed's benchmark rate is its main weapon for stabilizing consumer prices, which have crept up in recent months. The latest rate decision comes less than a week before Americans head to the polls for the midterm elections, where affordability issues will be top of mind for voters. President Trump has long urged the Fed to ease borrowing costs.
Stubborn inflation
During a press conference after the rate decision, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said economic indicators are moving in the right direction, citing robust consumer spending, a low unemployment rate and healthy overall economic growth.
He also said credit conditions — the terms lenders set for borrowing — have tightened for businesses and households since the Fed's September rate hike, a sign the economy is heading toward a "more durable period" of growth and price stability.
At the same time, he said inflation remains "too high" and acknowledged that the Fed hasn't yet succeeded in bringing inflation under control.
"On the employment side of the Fed's dual mandate, conditions are quite positive, and yet Americans, of course, are still dealing with inflation that has been running above the committee's objective for close to six years," he told reporters. "It's our responsibility to get inflation down."
Two dissents
Ten members of the Federal Open Market Committee, which sets interest rates, voted to hold the benchmark rate steady. Two FOMC members — Fed Board Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank President Beth Hammack — voted to raise it by 0.25 percentage points.
"We just came out of a heck of a family fight, a serious, sober discussion," Warsh said Wednesday. "I think we came to the right policy decision for this moment."
Investors and Wall Street analysts widely expected the Fed to remain on hold in October, but many economists think policymakers will raise rates at their last meeting of the year in December and again in 2027.
"The two hawkish dissents, the wording of the policy statement, and prior comments from officials all suggest the central bank will hike rates in December," Michael Pearce, chief U.S. economist for forecasting firm Oxford Economics, said in an email following the Fed's decision.
Samuel Tombs, chief U.S. economist at investment advisory firm Pantheon Macroeconomics, said financial markets are pricing in an additional 0.75 percentage points of tightening over the next year as the Fed tries to douse inflation.
Warsh stays tight-lipped
Warsh demurred when asked if Fed officials would raise rates at their Dec. 8-9 meeting, citing his stated reluctance to telegraph his policy views.
"A lot of things can happen, so I'm not going to be able to share with you my musings about what happens when this group gets together six weeks from now," he told a reporter.
The Iran war has kept global energy costs elevated, making it harder to bring down prices in the U.S. Last month, the closely watched Consumer Price Index rose at a 3.7% annual rate; core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 2.6% from a year ago. Both measures were above economists' expectations.
Solid economic growth and steady consumer spending are also exerting upward pressure on prices, complicating the task of taming inflation, according to economists.
What does this mean for your money?
The federal funds rate — what banks charge each other for overnight loans — influences the cost of borrowing across the U.S. economy. A rate hike can spur higher borrowing costs for bank loans, credit cards and auto loans, while boosting returns for savings accounts.
The Fed's pause in rate hikes could provide borrowers with some breathing room, Bankrate home lending expert Linda Bell said, citing potential relief for home equity rates. Still, consumers may be in for higher borrowing costs down the road. Matt Schulz, a chief consumer finance analyst at LendingTree, said it's possible some loan rates could continue to climb heading into the holiday shopping season.
"Even though the Fed is leaving rates alone this month, it might raise rates again at its last meeting of the year in December," Schulz said in an email ahead of the Fed's decision. "That is far from guaranteed, but it is something that Americans should be aware of. It means that the debt they run up during the holidays could get a little more expensive to pay off before the year ends, through no fault of their own."
A surprise change
While the Fed's decision to leave rates unchanged was widely expected, Warsh elicited surprise by announcing changes to the central bank's meeting schedule.
Policymakers will continue to meet eight times throughout the year. But starting in 2027, one of those meetings will be reserved for discussion and strategizing on monetary policy, Warsh said. At that meeting, the Fed will not vote on interest rates or issue a policy statement.
By 2028, Warsh said he expects two meetings to be dedicated to policy discussion and six to issuing rate decisions.
The change aligns with Warsh's broader vision for the Fed. He has been vocal in arguing for more limited communication from Fed officials, known as forward guidance, to preserve their flexibility in setting policy.
"Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular and information-rich intervals," he said. "But it's equally important we reserve time and space as an intellectually diverse group for strategic deliberations, for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons, focusing, as I say, on the left side of the decimal point."

- Total revenue for Q2 FY27 of $3.03 billion, down 4.0% YoY, down 4.0% on an organic basis(1)
- Q2 FY27 EBIT margin of 2.2%, and adjusted EBIT(2) margin of 6.2%
- Q2 FY27 Diluted earnings per share of $0.15; Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share(3) of $0.67, down 20.2% YoY
- Free cash flow(4) for the first half of FY27 was $405 million, compared to $337 million last year
- Q2 FY27 Bookings of $2.4 billion, trailing twelve month book to bill ratio of 1.0x
- Repurchased $60 million of shares
ASHBURN, Va., Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- DXC Technology (NYSE: DXC) today reported results for the second quarter fiscal 2027.
"On the quarter, we delivered revenue, adjusted EBIT, and Non-GAAP diluted EPS above our expectations, while making progress with the agentic and AI-based solutions that we expect will contribute to future growth. The revenue ramp for agentic solutions is more clear in terms of average deal size, close cycle timing, and pace of follow-on work," said Raul Fernandez, CEO of DXC Technology. "While our core revenue recovery will take time, I am confident that our role operating mission-critical systems gives DXC a differentiated position as enterprises look to deploy AI at scale."
Financial Highlights - Second Quarter Fiscal Year 2027
- Total revenue was $3.03 billion, down 4.0% year-over-year (down 4.0% on an organic basis).(1)
- EBIT was $66 million, down 52.2% year-over-year with a corresponding margin of 2.2%. Adjusted EBIT(2) was $187 million, down 26.4% year-over-year, with a corresponding margin(2) of 6.2%.
- Diluted earnings per share was $0.15. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share(3) was $0.67, down 20.2% year-over-year.
- Cash generated from operations was $217 million, down 46.9% year-over-year. Free cash flow(4) was $91 million, compared to $240 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2026. Free cash flow(4) for the first half of FY27 was $405 million, compared to $337 million last year.
- Bookings of $2.4 billion declined 10% year-over-year, with a book to bill ratio of 0.80x.
- Returned $60 million of capital to shareholders by repurchasing approximately 5.7 million shares.
- DXC acknowledges ongoing discussions regarding a possible sale of its insurance business.

Segment Highlights - Second Quarter Fiscal Year 2027
Consulting and Engineering Services ("CES")
- Revenue was $1,213 million, down 3.3% year-over-year (down 3.3% on an organic basis).(1)
- Segment profit was $125 million, down 13.8% year-over-year, with a corresponding margin of 10.3%.
- Bookings declined 17.0% year-over-year, with a book to bill ratio of 0.79x.
Global Infrastructure Services ("GIS")
- Revenue was $1,427 million, down 10.0% year-over-year (down 10.0% on an organic basis).(1)
- Segment profit was $66 million, down 45.9% year-over-year, with a corresponding margin of 4.6%.
- Bookings declined 12.7% year-over-year, with a book to bill ratio of 0.80x.
Insurance Software & Services ("Insurance")
- Revenue was $394 million, up 23.1% year-over-year (up 23.1% on an organic basis).(1) Organic revenue growth includes a favorable contract modification entered into during the second quarter of fiscal 2027.
- Segment profit was $45 million, up 60.7% year-over-year, with a corresponding margin of 11.4%.
- Bookings increased 43.5% year-over-year, with a book to bill ratio of 0.79x.
Full Fiscal Year 2027 and Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Guidance
Full Fiscal Year 2027
- Total revenue in the range of $11.91 billion and $11.98 billion, a decline of 5.5% to 5.0% year-over-year on an organic basis.(1)
- Adjusted EBIT margin(2) in the range of 5.75% to 6.25%.
- Non-GAAP diluted EPS(3) in the range of $2.25 to $2.50.
- Free Cash Flow(4) of ~$600 million.
Third Quarter Fiscal 2027
- Total revenue of ~$2.98 billion, a decline of ~6.0% year-over-year on an organic basis.(1)
- Adjusted EBIT margin(2) of ~6.0%.
- Non-GAAP Diluted EPS(3) of ~$0.55.

About DXC Technology
DXC Technology (NYSE: DXC) is a leading enterprise technology and innovation partner delivering software, services, and solutions to global enterprises and public sector organizations - helping them harness AI to drive outcomes at a time of exponential change with speed. With deep expertise in Managed Infrastructure Services, Application Modernization, and Industry-Specific Software Solutions, DXC modernizes, secures, and operates some of the world's most complex technology estates. Learn more at DXC.com.
Forward-Looking Statements
Except for historical information, statements in this document may constitute "forward-looking statements" based on our current assumptions regarding future performance. These statements involve numerous risks, uncertainties, and other factors outside our control that could cause actual results to differ materially, including: inability to effectively manage our sales organization, including execution, pipeline, and talent management; About Non-GAAP Measures
In an effort to provide investors with supplemental financial information, in addition to the preliminary and unaudited financial information presented on a GAAP basis, we also disclose in this press release preliminary non-GAAP information including: earnings before interest and taxes ("EBIT"), EBIT margin, adjusted EBIT, adjusted EBIT margin, non-GAAP diluted EPS, organic revenues, organic revenue growth, free cash flow, and non-GAAP tax rate.
We believe EBIT, adjusted EBIT, non-GAAP income before income taxes, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income attributable to DXC common stockholders, and non-GAAP EPS provide investors with useful supplemental information about our operating performance after excluding certain categories of expenses as well as gains and losses on certain dispositions and certain tax adjustments.
We believe constant currency revenues provides investors with useful supplemental information about our revenues after excluding the effect of currency exchange rate fluctuations for currencies other than U.S. dollars in the periods presented. See below for a description of the methodology we use to present constant currency revenues.
One category of expenses excluded from adjusted EBIT, non-GAAP income before income tax, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income attributable to DXC common stockholders, and non-GAAP EPS, incremental amortization of intangible assets acquired through business combinations, if included, may result in a significant difference in period over period amortization expense on a GAAP basis. We exclude amortization of certain acquired intangible assets as these non-cash amounts are inconsistent in amount and frequency and are significantly impacted by the timing and/or size of acquisitions. Although DXC management excludes amortization of acquired intangible assets, primarily customer-related intangible assets, from its non-GAAP expenses, we believe it is important for investors to understand that such intangible assets were recorded as part of purchase accounting and support revenue generation. Any future transactions may result in a change to the acquired intangible asset balances and associated amortization expense.
Another category of expenses excluded from adjusted EBIT, non-GAAP income before income tax, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income attributable to DXC common stockholders, and non-GAAP EPS is impairment losses, which, if included, may result in a significant difference in period-over-period expense on a GAAP basis. We exclude impairment losses as these non-cash amounts reflect generally an acceleration of what would be multiple periods of expense and are not expected to occur frequently. Further, assets such as goodwill may be significantly impacted by market conditions outside of management's control.
Selected references are made to revenue growth on an "organic basis" in order that certain financial results can be viewed without the impact of fluctuations in foreign currency rates and without the impacts of acquisitions and divestitures, thereby providing comparisons of operating performance from period to period of the business that we have owned during both periods presented. Organic revenue growth is calculated by dividing the year-over-year change in GAAP revenues attributed to organic growth by the GAAP revenues reported in the prior comparable period. Organic revenue is calculated as constant currency revenue excluding the impact of mergers, acquisitions or similar transactions until the one-year anniversary of the transaction and excluding revenues of divestitures during the reporting period. This approach is used for all results where the functional currency is not the U.S. dollar. We believe organic revenue growth provides investors with useful supplemental information about our revenues after excluding the effect of currency exchange rate fluctuations for currencies other than U.S. dollars and the effects of acquisitions and divestitures in both periods presented.
Free cash flow represents cash flow from operations, less capital expenditures. Free cash flow is utilized by our management, investors, and analysts to evaluate cash available for normal business operations, to pay debt, repurchase shares, and provide further investment in the business.
There are limitations to the use of the non-GAAP financial measures presented in this report. One of the limitations is that they do not reflect complete financial results. We compensate for this limitation by providing a reconciliation between our non-GAAP financial measures and the respective most directly comparable financial measure calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP. Additionally, other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate non-GAAP financial measures differently than we do, limiting the usefulness of those measures for comparative purposes between companies. Selected references are made on a "constant currency basis" so that certain financial results can be viewed without the impact of fluctuations in foreign currency rates, thereby providing comparisons of operating performance from period to period. Financial results on a "constant currency basis" are non-GAAP measures calculated by translating current period activity into U.S. Dollars using the comparable prior period's currency conversion rates. This approach is used for all results where the functional currency is not the U.S. Dollar.

Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures
Our non-GAAP adjustments include:
- Restructuring costs - includes costs, net of reversals, related to workforce and real estate optimization and other similar charges.
- Transaction, separation and integration-related ("TSI") costs - includes third party costs related to integration, separation, planning, financing and advisory fees and other similar charges associated with mergers, acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, and dispositions and other similar transactions incurred within one year of such transactions closing, except for costs associated with related disputes, which may arise more than one year after closing.
- Amortization of acquired intangible assets - includes amortization of intangible assets acquired through business combinations.
- Merger-related indemnification - represents the Company's estimate of potential net liability for tax related indemnifications.
- Gain on litigation award - reflects a gain related to the TCS Litigation judgment.
- Gains and losses on real estate and facility sales - gains and losses related to dispositions of real property.
- Gains and losses on dispositions - gains and losses related to dispositions of businesses, strategic assets and interests in less than wholly-owned entities.
- Impairment losses - non-cash charges associated with the permanent reduction in the value of the Company's assets (e.g., impairment of goodwill and other long-term assets including fixed assets and impairments to deferred tax assets for discrete changes in valuation allowances). Future discrete reversals of valuation allowances are likewise excluded.
- Tax adjustments - discrete tax adjustments to impair or recognize certain deferred tax assets, adjustments for changes in tax legislation and the impact of merger and divestitures. Income tax expense of all other (non-discrete) non-GAAP adjustments is based on the difference in the GAAP annual effective tax rate (AETR) and overall non-GAAP provision (consistent with the GAAP methodology).

title: Revenue gains take time to materialise even as Indian IT sees strong bookings
snippet: Indian IT firms post strong Q2 bookings, but revenue realization lags due to longer cycles and cost-conscious clients.
content:
India’s top IT services firms continued to report healthy deal wins in Q2 FY27, but the conversion of contracts into revenue remains a challenge, with longer implementation cycles and client focus on cost optimisation delaying the payoff from strong bookings.
During the quarter, HCLTech reported a total contract value (TCV) of $3.25 billion in new deal wins in Q2, up from $2.4 billion in Q1. TCS reported an order book TCV of $9.6 billion, compared with $9.5 billion in the previous quarter. Infosys reported large deal wins with a TCV of $5.2 billion, of which 62 per cent was net new business. The wins included a mega deal valued at more than $2 billion, taking the company’s large deal TCV up from $3.6 billion in the previous quarter.
Wipro’s total bookings stood at $2,595 million, down 22.9 per cent QoQ cc, while large deal bookings fell 58.6 per cent cc to $674 million. Tech Mahindra reported a TCV of $1,023 million, compared with $1,078 million in Q1, while its deal wins over the last 12 months rose 34.8 per cent year-on-year to $4.27 billion during the quarter.
During the company’s earnings conference call, TCS CEO and MD K Krithivasan said the company was confident of sustaining its growth momentum in the medium term, supported by its deal TCV, pipeline and ongoing client conversations.
Meanwhile, Wipro CEO and MD Srini Pallia said during the call that some deals were pushed into the current quarter as the contracts could not be signed on time in Q2.
“Both deals we could not sign will get signed. Our pipeline is robust. In addition to these two deals, we have a very strong pipeline for Q3. We are optimistic on the deals we have currently, which should give us revenue upside in Q4 as well. The focus currently is to close Q3 deals,” he said.
Despite demand returning this quarter and healthy deal signings, the top 5 firms reported close to $20 billion of bookings, less than Accenture’s $22 billion, Praveen Bhadada, CEO & Managing Director, Neovay Global, observed.
“Conversion is the issue. Infosys cut guidance in a strong deal quarter, Tech Mahindra’s twelve-month deal wins rose against 6.8% revenue growth, and TCS signed $9.6 billion but grew 0.2% sequentially. Today’s large deals run 5-10 years, focus on vendor consolidation and cost reduction, and pass AI productivity savings back to clients,” he said.
Biswajit Maity, Sr Principal Analyst at Gartner, noted that large-deal momentum remained strong during the quarter, reflecting continued demand for cost optimisation, modernisation, managed services and AI-led transformation initiatives.
“While strong deal activity is starting to support revenue growth, the impact is gradual because many large programs are still in the early stages of implementation. The nature of large deals is also evolving. Enterprises are increasingly signing outcome-based and AI-enabled contracts rather than traditional labour-based agreements, which means revenue is often realized over a longer period and tied to business outcomes, platform adoption, or AI usage,” he highlighted.
Maity said deal velocity has improved, with organisations accelerating AI, automation and modernisation projects backed by clear business cases. However, clients remain cost-conscious, favouring value-based pricing and flexible commercial models. While strong bookings signal demand, longer conversion cycles mean revenue benefits are likely to materialise over the coming quarters.
Published on October 25, 2026

title: Is Apple a Buy on the Dip, or Are Mounting Headwinds Too Strong?
snippet: Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) posted another strong quarter of iPhone sales when it reported its fiscal fourth-quarter results after ...
content:
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) posted another strong quarter of iPhone sales when it reported its fiscal fourth-quarter results after the bell on Nov. 2. However, the stock traded lower on worries of gross margin compression due to higher memory prices and decelerating service revenue growth.
The stock was up nearly 25% on the year before the report.
Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
Let's take a closer look at the company's fiscal Q4 results and prospects to see why I wouldn't be chasing this small pullback.
Strong iPhone sales
Apple's fiscal Q4 tends to be a seasonally weaker quarter for the company, as it comes right before the release of its newer model phone and before the holiday season. Its new iPhone 18 Pro was only available eight days in the quarter, while its new iPhone Duo didn't hit shelves until after the quarter was over. However, the company did benefit from the $100 price increase it implemented in June.
iPhone sales soared 17% to $57.58 billion, which was a September quarter record and ahead of the $56.54 billion analyst consensus, as compiled by LSEG. It saw strong double-digit iPhone sales in both the U.S. and Greater China, and set a record for upgraders worldwide. Meanwhile, it said the response to both the iPhone 18 and Duo has been strong.
Other product sales were mixed
Mac revenue was also strong, with sales climbing 24% year over year to $10.79 billion and topping analyst expectations for sales of $9.61 billion. The company credited strong growth in emerging markets. It set a September quarter record for new Mac customers.
Sales of Apple's other products were generally weak. Sales of iPads fell 10% to 6.23 billion, while wearable revenue sank by 8% to $8.3 billion. However, the company did recently launch new products in these categories, including a new iPad mini with an OLED display and Apple HomeView, which is meant to act as an entertainment and personal assistant hub.
Total product segment sales climbed by 12.5% to $82.9 billion. China was once again solid, with revenue jumping 21% to $17.54 billion.
Apple services revenue growth slows again
Apple's services segment -- which consists of its App Store, iCloud storage, Google Search revenue sharing, Apple Pay, Apple TV, and more -- saw revenue rise 10% to $31.57 billion. That was a continued deceleration from the 12% growth it saw in fiscal Q3 and 16% growth it saw in fiscal Q2. It was the segment's slowest quarterly growth since 2022.
Product gross margin came in at 37.2%, and excluding tariff refunds in both quarters was down 100 basis points sequentially. Like others in the space, Apple is currently dealing with surging memory prices. Service margin, meanwhile, rose by 40 basis points sequentially to 76%. Overall gross margin was 47.9%, which was above analyst expectations of 47.5%.
Overall, Apple's revenue rose by 12% to $114.48 billion, while its earnings per share (EPS) jumped 14% to $2.10. Excluding an $0.05 tariff rebate boost, adjusted EPS would have been $2.05. That topped the analyst consensus estimates for EPS of $1.99 on sales of $113.39 billion.
Tempered guidance
For fiscal Q1, Apple projected its revenue to grow by 7% to 10% year over year, impacted by currency headwinds and supply constraints. Service revenue is expected to increase between 8% to 9%, hurt by third-party licensing and currency headwinds. The company guided for gross margin to be between 45% and 46%.
Analysts were looking for revenue growth of 6%, but gross margins of 46.3%.
Time to stay on the sidelines
Apple has one of the best compounding business models in the world, but it is facing headwinds from memory prices, supply constraints, and currency headwinds. The company so far has been bucking the overall weakness in the smartphone and PC markets, but high memory prices are pressuring its gross margins. Another worry is the continued deceleration of the company's high-margin services business, which had been a consistent mid-teen revenue grower in the past.
Taken altogether, I would not be buying Apple on this minor dip. The stock continues to trade at a premium valuation despite its headwinds, with a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of nearly 35 times based on analysts' estimates for fiscal 2027 (which ends in September 2027).
The stock has benefited from huge multiple expansion over the past decade, but it's hard to see that continuing. As such, while Apple is a great company, I wouldn't be buying the stock right now.

title: Apple reports fourth quarter results
snippet: CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced financial results for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter ended September 26, 2026. The Company posted quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year ...
content:
PRESS RELEASE
                    
                    
                        November 2, 2026
                    
                    
                
            Apple reports fourth quarter results
                
                
                    September quarter records for total company revenue, iPhone revenue, and EPS 
 
Services revenue reaches new all-time high
        Services revenue reaches new all-time high
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced financial results for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter ended September 26, 2026. The Company posted quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year over year. Company gross margin was 47.9 percent, including a favorable impact of approximately 1 percentage point from tariff refunds. Diluted earnings per share was $2.10, up 14 percent year over year, and included a favorable impact of $0.05 from tariff refunds.
                 
             
                 “Today, Apple is proud to report a September quarter revenue record of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent from a year ago, with iPhone reaching a September quarter record and Services reaching an all-time high, capping off our best fiscal year ever,” said John Ternus, Apple’s CEO. “We’re closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet. That includes the iPhone Duo, the most transformational iPhone since the original, alongside iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, our most powerful iPhones yet. We also just introduced a whole new generation of hardware for the home and brought Touch to Mac for the first time. Together with the all-new Siri AI, it’s an incredible lineup to carry us into the holiday season.”
                 
             
                 “Apple delivered September quarter records for net income and EPS. Our record September quarter capped off a strong fiscal 2026, with all-time record revenue of $479 billion and double-digit EPS growth,” said Kevan Parekh, Apple’s CFO. “We generated $28 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, allowing us to return $28 billion to shareholders. Thanks to our very high levels of customer satisfaction and loyalty, our installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments.”
                 
             
                 Apple’s board of directors has declared a cash dividend of $0.27 per share of the Company’s common stock. The dividend is payable on November 16, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 12, 2026.
                 
             
                 Apple will provide live streaming of its Q4 2026 financial results conference call beginning at 2:00 p.m. PT on November 2, 2026, at apple.com/investor/earnings-call. The webcast will be available for replay for approximately two weeks thereafter.

| 2022 | $205.5B | $394.3B | 52.1% | FY2022 10-K | 
| 2023 | $200.6B | $383.3B | 52.3% | FY2023 10-K | 
| 2024 | $201.2B | $391.0B | 51.4% | FY2024 10-K | 
| 2025 | $209.6B | $416.2B | 50.4% | FY2025 10-K | 
| 2026 | $254.1B | $478.8B | 53.1% | FY2026 10-K | 
Apple’s fiscal year ends in late September, so fiscal 2026 ended on September 26, 2026. The iPhone 18 Pro went on sale eight days before that.
The same numbers are in our iPhone revenue share chart.
Photo via Sevela.p / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0) // The original iPhone produced $630 million of restated revenue in Apple’s fiscal 2007.
Where Apple changed how it reports
This series isn’t perfectly like for like, and the changes are worth knowing if you plan to quote it.
- Early iPhone revenue was spread over two years. Apple originally deferred iPhone revenue under subscription accounting, recognizing it over a 24-month estimated life. Its first 10-K showed only $123 million of iPhone revenue for fiscal 2007.
- In January 2010, Apple adopted new accounting rules retroactively and filed a 10-K/A. Fiscal 2007 iPhone revenue became $630 million, 2008 went from $1.8 billion to $6.7 billion, and 2009 from $6.8 billion to $13.0 billion. We use the restated figures.
- From fiscal 2013, Apple moved iPhone accessories into a separate Accessories line and restated 2012 and 2011. That cut 2012 from $80.5 billion to $78.7 billion. The 2007 to 2010 figures still include "related products and services".
- From fiscal 2019, Apple moved the value of Maps, Siri and free iCloud services bundled with devices into Services, and restated 2017 and 2018. 2018 iPhone revenue fell from $166.7 billion to $164.9 billion.
- Apple stopped reporting iPhone unit sales after fiscal 2018, so revenue is now the only official measure of iPhone’s scale.
- Fiscal 2012 and 2023 each had an extra week, a 53-week year that slightly flatters comparisons.
What happened in each era
The rise was remarkably fast. iPhone went from 2.6% of sales to more than half in five fiscal years, helped by carrier deals and international expansion. The peak came with the iPhone 6 and 6 Plus, when large screens and demand from China pushed fiscal 2015 sales up 52%.
Sales then fell 12% the following year. Since then, the percentage has been shaped less by iPhone weakness than by the growth of everything else. Services grew from $19.9 billion in fiscal 2015 to $123.3 billion in fiscal 2026, more than sixfold.
Fiscal 2026 broke the recent pattern. iPhone sales rose 21% to a record, and Apple’s filing credits higher sales of Pro models, lifting the iPhone’s share by almost three points. Our breakdown of the 2026 annual report has more on that year.
Photo via Apple Inc. // Pro models drove iPhone growth in Apple’s latest fiscal year.
Revenue isn’t profit
Apple doesn’t publish profit by product. It does report gross margin separately for Products and Services, and Services carries the higher margin. So iPhone’s share of Apple’s profit is likely to be lower than its 53% share of revenue would suggest, although Apple doesn’t give a figure. Be wary of any precise "iPhone profit share" number, because it is an estimate rather than something in these filings.
Questions this table answers
What percentage of Apple’s revenue comes from iPhone?
53.1% in fiscal 2026, up from 50.4% in fiscal 2025.
When was iPhone the largest share of Apple’s revenue?
Fiscal 2015, at 66.3%.
When did iPhone first pass half of Apple’s revenue?
Fiscal 2012, at 50.3% using restated figures.
Does Apple still report iPhone sales numbers?
It reports iPhone revenue, but it stopped reporting units after fiscal 2018.
How to read the trend
People have been predicting an Apple that no longer depends on the iPhone for years. These numbers show that hasn’t happened yet: for 15 straight fiscal years, more than half of the company’s sales have come from one product line. Services has grown into a very large business, but the iPhone remains the thing it is sold on top of.
Keep following what matters.
