title: Apple Statistics 2026: Revenue, iPhone, and Services | Fin Loom
snippet: Oct 4, 2026 · Apple statistics for 2026 covering revenue, iPhone, Services, margins, installed devices, geographic growth, and the changing business mix.
content:
Apple Statistics 2026: Revenue, iPhone, Services, and the Changing Business Mix
Apple is often measured by the number of iPhones it sells. That is no longer enough. The company has become a mix of hardware, software, and subscriptions, built on an installed base that supports recurring revenue long after the initial device sale.
The Apple statistics worth watching therefore focus on the relationship between products and Services. Hardware brings users into the ecosystem, and Services then monetize the relationship over time. In fiscal 2026, both sides of that model have been producing record results.
Key Takeaways
- First-quarter revenue: Apple generated $143.8 billion in revenue in fiscal Q1 2026, up from $124.3 billion a year earlier.
- Second-quarter revenue: Fiscal Q2 2026 revenue reached $111.2 billion, up 17% year over year.
- Third-quarter revenue: Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue reached $109.4 billion, up 16%.
- Services: Services revenue reached a record $30.0 billion in fiscal Q1 2026.
- iPhone: iPhone revenue reached $85.3 billion in fiscal Q1 2026.
- Installed base: Apple's installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high by Q3 2026.
- Gross margin: Gross margin reached 50.1% in fiscal Q3 2026, though Apple noted a favorable impact of about two percentage points from tariff refunds.
- Recurring revenue: Services are strategically important because they increase recurring monetization from the installed device base.
Apple Statistics at a Glance
The table gathers the headline Apple statistics from Apple's first-quarter financial statements and its second-quarter and third-quarter results.
| Metric | Figure | Period | 
|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | $143.8B | Fiscal Q1 2026 | 
| Products revenue | $113.7B | Fiscal Q1 2026 | 
| Services revenue | $30.0B | Fiscal Q1 2026 | 
| iPhone revenue | $85.3B | Fiscal Q1 2026 | 
| Net income | $42.1B | Fiscal Q1 2026 | 
| Q2 revenue | $111.2B | Fiscal Q2 2026 | 
| Q3 revenue | $109.4B | Fiscal Q3 2026 | 
| Q3 gross margin | 50.1% | Fiscal Q3 2026 | 
Apple Generated $143.8 Billion in Fiscal Q1 2026
Apple's quarter ended December 27, 2025 produced $143.756 billion in net sales. That was up from $124.3 billion in the comparable prior-year quarter.
Net income reached $42.1 billion. This was an exceptionally strong holiday quarter.
But the more interesting statistic is the mix. Products generated $113.7 billion, while Services generated $30.0 billion. The Services component is now large enough to count independently. Apple Pay also competes with PayPal in digital wallets, and PayPal statistics cover that rival's scale.
iPhone Revenue Reached $85.3 Billion
iPhone remained Apple's largest product category. Fiscal Q1 2026 iPhone revenue was $85.269 billion, up from $69.138 billion a year earlier.
That is enormous concentration. The iPhone remains the primary gateway into the Apple ecosystem. It also creates demand for:
- App Store purchases
- iCloud
- Apple Music
- Apple TV
- Apple Pay
- Accessories
- Warranties
- Other services
For this reason, iPhone economics extend beyond the hardware sale.
Services Revenue Reached $30.0 Billion in Q1
Services revenue was $30.013 billion in fiscal Q1 2026. That compares with $26.340 billion a year earlier.
The category includes a broad mix of recurring and transactional revenue. Services count because they generally require less physical manufacturing than hardware. That can support attractive margins and recurring cash flow.
Fiscal Q2 Revenue Increased 17%
Apple reported $111.2 billion in fiscal Q2 2026 revenue, up 17% year over year. The company described it as its best March quarter ever. iPhone set a March-quarter revenue record, and Services reached another all-time high. The result showed that the strong holiday quarter was not simply a one-quarter event.
Fiscal Q3 Revenue Reached $109.4 Billion
Apple reported $109.4 billion in fiscal Q3 2026 revenue, up 16%. The quarter set new June-quarter records for company revenue and earnings per share.
Apple also said iPhone, Mac, and Services each set June-quarter revenue records. This broad growth is important. A company already generating more than $100 billion in quarterly revenue is still producing double-digit year-over-year growth.
Apple's Installed Base Keeps Expanding
Apple said its installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments in fiscal Q3 2026. This statistic is strategically important even without a current exact device count in the release.
The installed base determines the size of the audience Apple can monetize through Services. A larger installed base can support:
- Subscriptions
- Payments
- Cloud storage
- App purchases
- Accessories
- Upgrades
- Financing
Services Change the Quality of Revenue
Hardware revenue is naturally cyclical. Consumers do not buy a new phone every month.
Services can generate recurring revenue throughout the ownership period. That creates a flywheel:
device sale → installed base → recurring services → ecosystem retention → future device replacement
The model makes Apple less dependent on a single hardware purchase.
Apple Revenue by Product Category
Among recent Apple statistics, fiscal Q1 2026 gives a clear snapshot of the product mix.
| Category | Revenue | 
|---|---|
| iPhone | $85.27B | 
| Services | $30.01B | 
| Wearables, Home and Accessories | $11.49B | 
| iPad | $8.60B | 
| Mac | $8.39B | 
In these Apple statistics, the table shows both concentration and diversification. iPhone dominates, while Services provide a substantial second engine. In addition, the remaining hardware businesses are each large enough to represent major companies on their own.
Geographic Revenue Is Broad
Fiscal Q1 2026 sales were:
| Region | Revenue | 
|---|---|
| Americas | $58.53B | 
| Europe | $38.15B | 
| Greater China | $25.53B | 
| Rest of Asia Pacific | $12.14B | 
| Japan | $9.41B | 
This geographic diversity reduces dependence on any single market. It also creates currency, regulation, tariff, and geopolitical exposure. Greater China remains especially important because of both revenue scale and competition.
Gross Margin Reached 50.1% in Q3 2026
Apple reported a 50.1% gross margin in fiscal Q3 2026. The company noted that this included a favorable effect of roughly two percentage points from tariff refunds.
That qualification is important. Investors should separate recurring economics from temporary items.
Even after adjustment, Apple's gross-margin profile remains exceptionally strong for a company that sells massive quantities of physical hardware. Services contribute materially to that result.
Net Income Shows the Profit Scale
Fiscal Q1 2026 net income was $42.1 billion. That is more profit in one quarter than many large companies generate in years.
The scale supports: research and development, capital expenditure, acquisitions, dividends, share repurchases, and cash reserves. Apple's profitability is one reason its stock is often analyzed as a quality compounder rather than simply a hardware manufacturer.
Buybacks Count Because Apple's Share Count Is Falling
Apple has returned enormous amounts of capital through share repurchases. When a company buys back shares, each remaining share represents a slightly larger ownership claim if the repurchases exceed stock issuance.
This can increase earnings per share even when net income grows more slowly. Investors should therefore compare net income growth, EPS growth, and diluted share-count change. EPS should not be read as though all growth came from the business.
Apple Pay Extends the Ecosystem Into Payments
Apple Pay strengthens Apple's position beyond devices. It makes the iPhone a payment credential.
This deepens daily engagement and places Apple inside the checkout experience. The payment economics differ from a pure payment processor such as PayPal, but the strategic value is clear. Apple does not need to become a bank to increase its role in financial transactions.
Services Revenue Is Not One Business
The Services category contains different revenue types. It can include the following:
- App Store economics
- iCloud
- Apple Music
- Apple TV
- AppleCare
- Advertising
- Payments
- Subscriptions
- Licensing arrangements
These have different margins and growth drivers. That means total Services growth is useful but incomplete. Investors should also pay attention to regulation affecting app distribution, payments, and platform rules.
Regulation Could Change Platform Economics
Apple faces regulatory scrutiny in multiple jurisdictions. Issues include App Store commissions, third-party app distribution, default apps, payment rules, competition, and interoperability.
These is important can affect Services economics even if hardware sales remain strong. This is why the quality of Apple's earnings depends partly on platform regulation.
AI Is Becoming Part of the Product Cycle
Apple's 2026 announcements have placed greater emphasis on AI software and Siri. Unlike hyperscale cloud vendors, Apple monetizes AI partly through devices and ecosystem retention rather than selling infrastructure directly. The cloud providers' side of that contrast is covered in AI capital spending by big tech.
The investment thesis is therefore different. AI may help Apple: increase device upgrade demand, strengthen ecosystem loyalty, improve Services, and differentiate hardware. The financial evidence should be measured through product demand and monetization rather than AI narrative alone.
Product Mix Affects Margins
Not every dollar of Apple revenue has the same margin. Services typically carry different economics from devices.
Product mix therefore affects gross margin. If Services grows faster than hardware, total company margin can benefit.
If lower-margin products grow faster, the opposite can occur. This is why fundamental analysis looks at company performance through revenue mix and margin quality rather than only total sales growth.
Apple's Business Model Creates Recurring Upgrade Cycles
A user may buy an iPhone every several years. During the period between purchases, Apple can still earn through Services and accessories.
Then the next hardware cycle begins. This repeat behavior gives Apple a customer-lifetime-value model different from a one-time electronics company. The installed base is therefore economically more important than annual unit sales alone.
The iPhone Concentration Risk Has Not Disappeared
Diversification has improved. Even so, iPhone is still dominant.
Fiscal Q1 2026 iPhone revenue represented roughly 59% of total company revenue. A major decline in iPhone demand would therefore remain material. The Services business reduces concentration but does not eliminate it.
Apple's Revenue Quality Comes From Ecosystem Depth
Two companies can report the same hardware revenue with very different long-term economics. Apple's advantage is the relationship that follows the sale.
The device can lead to paid storage, app spending, subscriptions, payments, accessories, service plans, and eventual replacement. That creates recurring monetization around a durable installed base. The deeper the ecosystem relationship, the more valuable each device customer becomes over time.
Greater China Remains Both Opportunity and Risk
Greater China produced more than $25 billion in fiscal Q1 2026 revenue. That is economically material.
It also exposes Apple to local smartphone competition, regulation, geopolitics, supply-chain policy, consumer sentiment, and currency movements. A diversified geographic footprint does not eliminate concentration risk inside a strategically important market. Investors should therefore monitor both regional revenue and competitive share.
Apple's Margin Mix Is Unusual for Hardware
Traditional electronics manufacturing often carries modest margins. Apple's combination of premium hardware, direct distribution, ecosystem lock-in, and Services creates a different profile. Services can lift consolidated gross margin, and premium devices can support pricing.
Scale improves procurement and supply-chain bargaining power. This helps explain why Apple's margin structure looks different from many hardware peers.
Research and Development Has Become More Important
Apple spent heavily on R&D in fiscal Q1 2026. The company must invest across:
- Silicon
- Operating systems
- AI
- Health
- Spatial computing
- Services
- Security
- Devices
R&D is not capitalized in the same way as data-center capex. Much of it flows through operating expense. That means Apple's innovation spending affects the income statement differently from hyperscale infrastructure spending.
Installed Base Is a Better Strategic Metric Than Annual Unit Sales Alone
Apple no longer regularly reports iPhone unit sales. This has frustrated some analysts.
The installed base may be more strategically useful. A user who keeps an iPhone for four years still generates potential Services revenue during the entire period.
Unit shipments measure acquisition and replacement. Installed devices measure the population available for monetization. Both are important, but they answer different questions.
Services Regulation Could Affect Margins Before Revenue
Changes to app distribution or payment rules may not immediately reduce the number of Apple users. They can still change economics.
If developers gain alternative payment options or distribution channels, Apple's commission structure can face pressure. That may show up first in margin or Services growth rather than device sales. Investors should therefore connect regulatory developments to the specific revenue streams affected.
Apple Generates Value From Customer Retention
Apple's ecosystem economics depend heavily on retention. A customer who remains in the ecosystem can buy multiple generations of devices while also paying for Services.
Retention reduces the need to reacquire the same customer from scratch. It also increases the economic value of the installed base. Investors should therefore think about Apple through customer lifetime value as well as annual product sales.
Upgrade Cycles Can Shift Quarterly Revenue
iPhone demand is not evenly distributed. New product launches create seasonal peaks.
Replacement cycles can lengthen when devices remain useful for more years. They can shorten when a major feature creates stronger upgrade demand.
This makes quarterly hardware comparisons sensitive to timing. A better long-term analysis uses several product cycles rather than one launch window.
Services Can Stabilize Hardware Cyclicality
A device cycle may weaken while Services continue growing. That can soften the financial impact of slower unit demand.
The effect is not unlimited. Services depend on the installed base that hardware created.
But recurring monetization gives Apple a buffer that a pure hardware vendor does not have. This is one reason the growth of Services has changed how investors value the business.
Capital Returns Influence Per-Share Growth
Apple has spent heavily on share repurchases for years. When shares are retired, the denominator used for earnings per share falls.
That means EPS can grow faster than net income. Investors should separate: growth in total profit, reduction in share count, and resulting EPS growth. Both can benefit shareholders, but they come from different economic sources.
Supply Chain Risk Remains Material
Apple depends on a complex global manufacturing system. Its products require advanced semiconductors, displays, cameras, batteries, components, assembly, shipping, and logistics.
Geopolitical tensions, tariffs, natural disasters, and supplier disruptions can affect both cost and availability. The company's scale provides purchasing power.
It also creates concentration because very large production volumes must be supported reliably. Supply-chain diversification therefore has strategic value even when it increases near-term cost.
Hardware Innovation Still Supports Services Growth
Services cannot expand indefinitely without a compelling device ecosystem. New hardware brings additional users and encourages existing customers to stay.
Features that increase device utility can also increase: cloud storage, app purchases, media subscriptions, payments, and accessories. The relationship is circular.
Hardware supports Services, and Services in turn make hardware harder to leave. That is the core of Apple's ecosystem economics.
Final Perspective
Apple statistics show a business that still depends heavily on iPhone, but increasingly monetizes customers long after the hardware purchase. That creates two engines.
Hardware expands and refreshes the installed base. Services increase the economic value of that base. The strength of Apple's future results will depend on maintaining both sides of the system while managing regulation, product cycles, geographic competition, and the cost of integrating AI into the ecosystem.
Fiscal 2026 So Far and What Apple Has Said About the Outlook
Three fiscal 2026 quarters are now reported. Added together, they give a nine-month view.
What Has Been Reported
The table lists each reported quarter of fiscal 2026.
| Fiscal 2026 quarter | Revenue | Change from prior year | 
|---|---|---|
| First quarter, ended December 27, 2025 | $143.8 billion | Up from $124.3 billion | 
| Second quarter | $111.2 billion | +17% | 
| Third quarter, ended June 27, 2026 | $109.4 billion | +16% | 
| Nine months, summed | About $364.4 billion | Not stated by Apple | 
The nine-month total is a sum of the three reported quarters, not a figure Apple published. In the third quarter, diluted earnings per share were $2.02, up 29% from a year earlier.
Apple declared a cash dividend of $0.27 per share. It said iPhone and Services revenue set June-quarter records and that the installed base of active devices reached a new high. Chief financial officer Kevan Parekh said, “Our installed base of active devices also reached a new all-time high.”
What Apple Projects
Apple's third-quarter release contains no revenue or earnings guidance. Any projection for the fourth quarter or for fiscal 2027 attributed to Apple should be checked against the company's own statements.
Many Apple statistics pages mix reported results with analyst estimates of shipments and future revenue. The figures on this page are reported results only.
The fourth fiscal quarter will complete the fiscal 2026 picture. Until Apple reports it, a full-year figure is an estimate, not a result.
Frequently Asked Questions
How Much Revenue Does Apple Make?
In fiscal 2026 so far, Apple reported $143.8 billion in the first quarter, $111.2 billion in the second, and $109.4 billion in the third.
How Much Revenue Comes From the iPhone?
iPhone revenue was $85.3 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, up from $69.1 billion a year earlier. That was roughly 59% of Apple's total revenue.
How Much Revenue Does Apple Services Generate?
Services generated $30.0 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, up from $26.3 billion a year earlier, and Apple reported further Services records later in the year.
Is Apple Still Growing?
Yes. Fiscal 2026 second-quarter revenue rose 17% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue rose 16%. Third-quarter earnings per share rose 29% to $2.02.
Why Are Services Important to Apple?
Services let Apple earn recurring and transactional revenue from devices already in use. That reduces its dependence on new hardware sales and supports its gross margin.

title: Apple Services Revenue Statistics 2026: $109,158 Million a Year at a 75.4% Gross Margin
snippet: Oct 3, 2026 · Apple Services earned $109,158 million in fiscal 2025 at a 75.4% gross margin, about a quarter of sales and two-fifths of gross profit. The yearly and quarterly figures, from Apple filings and newsroom releases.
content:
Apple’s Services business generated $109,158 million in net sales in fiscal 2025, up 14% from fiscal 2024, according to Apple’s Form 10-K. The same filing puts the Services gross margin percentage at 75.4%, against 36.8% for Products. Those two figures anchor the Apple services revenue statistics below.
Services net sales reached $30,739 million in the quarter ended June 27, 2026, up from $27,423 million a year earlier. Across the first nine months of fiscal 2026, Services net sales rose 14.1% year over year. Every figure below comes from Apple’s own filings and newsroom, which report Services as a single line.
Key Takeaways
- Services made up 26.2% of Apple’s fiscal 2025 net sales, yet it produced 42.2% of the company’s gross margin.
- Services net sales grew 59.5% between fiscal 2021 and fiscal 2025, from a base of $68,425 million.
- The gap between Services and Products gross margin percentage reached 38.6 percentage points in fiscal 2025.
- Services net sales rose 14.1% in the first nine months of fiscal 2026.
- Mac, iPad, and Wearables, Home and Accessories together sold $97,417 million in fiscal 2025, less than Services on its own.
- Apple’s Services gross margin percentage was 75.6% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, flat compared to the third quarter of 2025, according to Apple’s third-quarter Form 10-Q.
Editor’s Choice
- Fiscal 2025 Services net sales: $109,158 million, against total net sales of $416,161 million.
- Fiscal 2025 Services gross margin: $82,314 million, according to Apple’s annual report.
- Second quarter fiscal 2026 Services net sales: $30,976 million, which Apple called a new all-time high.
- Nine-month fiscal 2026 Services net sales: $91,728 million, against $80,408 million a year earlier.
- Nine-month fiscal 2026 Services gross margin percentage: 76.3%, up from 75.5%. Services gross margin increased during the first nine months of 2026.
- App Store ecosystem in 2025: over $1.4 trillion in developer billings and sales, according to a new study by economists at Analysis Group.
Apple Services Revenue Statistics by Fiscal Year
About This Data
Figures come from 17 Apple documents: 9 SEC filings and 8 Apple Newsroom releases. Shares and growth rates are calculated from those figures.
- Services net sales rose 14% in fiscal 2022, and Services reached $78,129 million that year. Services net sales increased 9%, or $7.1 billion, during 2023 due to higher net sales across all lines of business.
- Services growth reached 13% in fiscal 2024 and 14% in fiscal 2025, while total net sales grew 2% and 6%.
- Apple’s annual Services net sales rose by $40,733 million between fiscal 2021 and fiscal 2025.
- Services accounted for 18.7% of net sales in fiscal 2021, against 26.2% in fiscal 2025.
- Apple’s Services net sales include amortization of the deferred value of services bundled in the sales price of certain products, so some Services revenue arrives with device sales.
- Apple attributed the fiscal 2025 increase primarily to higher net sales from advertising, the App Store and cloud services.
| About This Data |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Fiscal year | Services net sales ($ millions) | Total net sales ($ millions) | 
|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 68,425 | 365,817 | 
| 2022 | 78,129 | 394,328 | 
| 2023 | 85,200 | 383,285 | 
| 2024 | 96,169 | 391,035 | 
| 2025 | 109,158 | 416,161 | 
Source: Apple Form 10-K, fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2023
Apple Services Revenue by Quarter
- Fourth-quarter fiscal 2025 Services net sales reached $28,750 million, up 15.1% year over year, a result Apple described as an all-time revenue record for Services. The device base behind that revenue shows in the Apple ecosystem lock-in data.
- In the December 2025 quarter, Services achieved an all-time revenue record of $30,013 million, up 14% from $26,340 million a year earlier.
- March 2026 quarter Services net sales rose 16.3% year over year, to $30,976 million from $26,645 million.
- June 2026 quarter growth slowed to 12.1%, with Services net sales of $30,739 million against $27,423 million a year earlier, although iPhone, Mac and Services revenue set new June quarter records.
- Services net sales slipped by $237 million between the March and June 2026 quarters.
- The three fiscal 2026 quarters reported so far total $91,728 million.
View the data
Recent Developments
- September 21, 2026: Apple announced the opening of Apple Music Hall, a live music venue in London’s Battersea Power Station.
- September 15, 2026: Apple TV landed 29 wins at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, including 14 for Widow’s Bay.
- September 8, 2026: Apple said Pusheen’s Place launches exclusively on Apple Arcade on October 1, with River City Survivors, Terraria+, Touchgrind BMX 2+, and 4 Pics 1 Word+ also joining the service. Arcade titles also reach Mac players, a market covered in Mac gaming statistics.
- Third-quarter Form 10-Q: Apple’s fiscal 2026 filing said Services net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales from advertising and cloud services.
- July 30, 2026: Apple posted quarterly revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16% year over year, with CEO Tim Cook citing “double-digit revenue growth across iPhone, Mac and Services, and in every geographic segment.”
- June 4, 2026: Apple said the App Store ecosystem facilitated over $1.4 trillion in developer billings and sales in 2025, citing a study by economists at Analysis Group.
Apple Services Gross Margin Percentage
- Apple’s total gross margin percentage was 46.9% in fiscal 2025, 46.2% in fiscal 2024 and 44.1% in fiscal 2023.
- Apple’s Services gross margin percentage rose to 75.4% in fiscal 2025 from 73.9% in fiscal 2024.
- Apple said the fiscal 2025 increase came primarily from a different mix of services, partially offset by higher costs.
- Apple’s Services gross margin percentage decreased during 2023 compared to 2022.
- Between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2025, the Services margin percentage gained 4.6 percentage points.
- Apple’s Products gross margin percentage slipped to 36.8% in fiscal 2025 from 37.2%, which Apple linked to a different mix of products and tariff costs.

| Fiscal year | Services gross margin (%) | Products gross margin (%) | 
|---|---|---|

| 2022 | 71.7 | 36.3 | 
| 2023 | 70.8 | 36.5 | 
| 2024 | 73.9 | 37.2 | 
| 2025 | 75.4 | 36.8 | 
Source: Apple Form 10-K, fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2023
Apple Services Gross Profit vs Products
- Services produced 31.2% of Apple’s gross margin in fiscal 2021, against 42.2% in fiscal 2025.
- Services gross margin in dollars grew 72.5% from fiscal 2021 to fiscal 2025.
- Products gross margin grew 7.4% over the same four years.
- Services cost of sales was $26,844 million in fiscal 2025, up from $25,119 million, while Products cost of sales reached $194,116 million.
- Apple said the fiscal 2025 rise in Services gross margin came primarily from higher Services net sales and a different mix of services.
- Total gross margin reached $195,201 million in fiscal 2025, up from $180,683 million in fiscal 2024.
View the data
By the numbers: Apple’s fiscal 2025 Form 10-K reports Services gross margin of $82,314 million against $112,887 million for Products, on Services net sales of $109,158 million and total net sales of $416,161 million. A business with about a quarter of the revenue now earns roughly two-fifths of Apple’s gross profit.
Apple Services Gross Margin by Quarter
- Services gross margin was $22,966 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, against $19,762 million a year earlier.
- The second quarter delivered $23,752 million, up from $20,183 million.
- Third-quarter Services gross margin reached $23,245 million, against $20,725 million a year earlier.
- Apple said Services gross margin increased primarily due to higher Services net sales and a different mix of services, partially offset by higher costs.
- Services cost of sales rose to $7,494 million in the June 2026 quarter from $6,698 million.
- Company gross margin was 50.1% in that quarter, including a favorable impact of approximately 2 percentage points from tariff refunds.
View the data
Apple Revenue Breakdown: Services vs Hardware
- Products net sales were $307,003 million in fiscal 2025, or 2.8 times the Services figure.
- Services revenue equaled 52.1% of iPhone revenue in fiscal 2025.
- Services was 20.9% of net sales in the holiday quarter ended December 27, 2025.
- That share rose to 28.1% in the June 2026 quarter.
- Mac net sales grew 12% and iPad 5% in fiscal 2025, while Wearables, Home and Accessories fell 4%. The Mac trend has its own page of Apple Mac sales figures.
View the data
Quarter by quarter, the next chart sets iPhone net sales beside Services across the same fiscal periods.
View the data
What is Apple’s largest source of revenue?
iPhone net sales were $209,586 million in fiscal 2025, out of total net sales of $416,161 million, or 50.4% of the total. That makes iPhone Apple’s largest source of revenue, with Services second at about a quarter of sales.
Apple Services Revenue Growth in Fiscal 2026
- Services net sales reached $60,989 million in the first six months of fiscal 2026, against $52,985 million a year earlier.
- Apple’s first-quarter Form 10-Q credited higher net sales from advertising, the App Store and cloud services.
- The second-quarter filing named the same three drivers: advertising, the App Store and cloud services.
- The third-quarter filing said Services net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales from advertising and cloud services. The App Store dropped out of the named drivers in the quarter growth slowed.
- Nine-month Services net sales rose by $11,320 million year over year.
- Services supplied 39.1% of Apple’s gross margin in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, down from 41.3% in the first nine months of fiscal 2025.

|---|---|---|
| Services net sales ($ millions) | 91,728 | 80,408 | 
| Services cost of sales ($ millions) | 21,765 | 19,738 | 
| Services gross margin ($ millions) | 69,963 | 60,670 | 
| Services gross margin (%) | 76.3 | 75.5 | 
Source: Apple Form 10-Q and quarterly financial statements, third quarter fiscal 2026
Key finding: Apple’s Form 10-Q filings for fiscal 2026 name advertising, the App Store and cloud services as the Services drivers in the first quarter, but only advertising and cloud services in the third. Advertising and cloud storage now carry the growth story Apple tells investors.
What Apple Services Includes
- Apple’s advertising services include third-party licensing arrangements and the Company’s own advertising platforms.
- AppleCare is a portfolio of fee-based service and support products.
- Apple’s cloud services store and keep customers’ content up-to-date and available across multiple Apple devices and Windows personal computers.
- Digital content runs through platforms including the App Store and subscription services including Apple Arcade, Apple Fitness+, Apple Music, Apple News+ and Apple TV.
- Payment services include Apple Card, a co-branded credit card, and Apple Pay.
- The Apple filings cited here report these lines as one Services number, with no separate App Store, Apple Music, Apple TV or iCloud revenue. Bundles such as Setapp and one-off app purchases compete for the same spend.

| Service line | What Apple’s Form 10-K includes | 
|---|---|

| Payment services | Apple Card and Apple Pay | 
Source: Apple Form 10-K, fiscal 2025
Apple Net Sales by Geographic Segment
- Europe net sales grew 10% in fiscal 2025, Japan 15%, and the Americas 7%.
- Greater China net sales declined 4% in fiscal 2025, after falling 7.7% in fiscal 2024.
- Apple said Americas net sales increased during 2025 primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone and Services.
- Total net sales across all segments were $416,161 million, the same total as the category table.

Worth noting: Apple’s fiscal 2025 Form 10-K reports Americas net sales of $178,353 million and Europe net sales of $111,032 million for the year. Those totals cover all products and services, and the Apple filings cited here report no Services revenue by region.
App Store Ecosystem Statistics
- The App Store saw over 850 million average weekly users spanning 175 countries and regions.
- For more than 90% of the billings and sales facilitated by the App Store ecosystem, developers did not pay any commission to Apple.
- Since 2019, the size of the App Store ecosystem has nearly tripled.
- In 2025, more than 40 of the top 100 apps on the storefront featured consumer-facing AI capabilities.
- These are sales through apps, not Apple revenue. Mac developers can also sell outside the store, as Mac App Store versus direct downloads explains.
| App Store Ecosystem Statistics |  | 
|---|---|
| App Store ecosystem component, 2025 | Billings and sales facilitated | 
|---|---|
| Total ecosystem | over $1.4 trillion | 
| Physical goods and services | $1.1 trillion | 
| In-app advertising | $151 billion | 
| Digital goods and services | $149 billion | 
Source: Apple Newsroom, Analysis Group study, June 2026
Legal and Regulatory Pressure on Apple Services
- Apple earns revenue from licensing arrangements with Google and other companies to offer their search services on its platforms and applications.
- On September 2, 2025, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia ordered certain remedies after Google was found to have violated U.S. antitrust laws.
- That order is subject to further proceedings, which may change how the remedies are interpreted or applied.
- The European Commission’s Article 5(4) investigation relates to how developers may communicate and promote offers to end users for apps distributed through the App Store.
View the data
Does Google pay Apple for search?
Yes, though the Apple filings cited here do not state the amount. Apple earns revenue from licensing arrangements with Google and other companies to offer their search services, according to its latest Form 10-Q. The fiscal 2025 Form 10-K places third-party licensing arrangements inside advertising services.
How much does Apple make from the App Store?
The Apple filings cited here report no App Store revenue. The App Store is one of the digital content platforms Apple’s Form 10-K lists under Services. They give Services only as a total, $109,158 million for fiscal 2025.
The $1.4 trillion figure Apple publicizes is ecosystem billings and sales, and for more than 90% of it developers paid no commission to Apple.
What is the outlook for Apple services in 2026 and 2027?
The Apple releases and filings cited here give no Services forecast. Apple’s third-quarter fiscal 2026 Form 10-Q says the Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure. The fiscal 2025 Form 10-K carries the same caution about gross margins.
Services net sales grew 14.1% in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, and the Services gross margin percentage was flat year over year in the third quarter. Apple’s fourth-quarter release will set the full fiscal 2026 total.
Conclusion
Services reached $109,158 million in fiscal 2025, and its gross margin percentage was 75.4%, against 36.8% for Products. That margin lets about a quarter of Apple’s sales deliver roughly two-fifths of its gross profit.
The Apple filings and releases cited here report no App Store, Apple Music or iCloud revenue and no Services split by region. Anyone comparing Apple’s subscription services against Spotify or tracking Mac market share trends should treat finer breakdowns as outside estimates.

Started in 1976, Apple has emerged as one of the world’s most influential and recognizable brands. The company increased the rise of smartphones with the iPhone.
By 2021, Apple was valued at over $2 trillion, marking itself the most valuable tech company. As of the year 2024, the company generated $392.4 billion. (Updated 17th Jan 2025)
Keep reading about Apple’s past and present sales figures to better understand its business.
Apple Key Statistics

- An estimated 1 billion iPhones, 72 million iPads, and 30 million Mac and MacBook units were sold in 2022.
- In 2021, Apple’s home and wearable division grew by 25%.
- Apple Music has an estimated ~120 million paid subscribers in 2026.
Apple Overview
- Date Founded: 1 April 1976
- Headquarters: Cupertino, California
- People: Tim Cook, Jeff Williams, Craig Federighi, and Eddy Cue

Ever since its launch in 2008, iPhone has been Apple’s most valuable product. In fact, it was the main source of revenue.
But later, Apple diversified itself into other product lines, including AirPods, services, and watches. Still, the iPhone generates 50% of the total revenue.
From the year 2008 to 2015, iPhone saw massive growth in its sales. But the revenue of this product stagnated for five years. Hopefully, iPhone’s popularity will increase revenue by 39% in 2021.
As of 2024, the iPhone is one of the top choices of people, with 202 billion in revenue.

title: Apple Statistics 2026
snippet: May 1, 2026 · Apple hit a record $143.8B in Q1 2026 revenue with a 16% YoY increase and over 2.5 billion active devices worldwide. Explore the latest Apple stats, including iPhone sales, market share, services growth, and regional performance.
content:
Apple posted record revenue of $143.8 billion in fiscal Q1 2026, up 16% year over year, while its installed base crossed 2.5 billion active devices. This article covers the latest Apple statistics for 2026, including revenue, iPhone sales, market share, services growth, and regional performance.
Apple Statistics 2026: Top 5 Numbers
- Apple recorded $143.8 billion in fiscal Q1 2026 revenue, up 16% year over year.
- The active device installed base reached 2.5 billion in January 2026.
- iPhone revenue hit an all-time quarterly high of $85.3 billion, up 23% year over year.
- Services revenue reached a record $30 billion in Q1 2026, growing 14% annually.
- Apple shipped 247.8 million iPhones globally in 2025, ranking first by unit shipments.
Apple Revenue Statistics 2026
Apple reported $143.8 billion in revenue for fiscal Q1 2026, the quarter ending December 27, 2025. That figure is up from $124.3 billion in the same quarter a year earlier. Net income reached $42.1 billion, or $2.84 per diluted share, up 19% year over year.
For the March 2026 quarter, Apple guided revenue growth between 13% and 16%, putting the range at $107.8 billion to $110.7 billion.
| Metric | Q1 FY2026 | Q1 FY2025 | YoY Change | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Total Revenue | $143.8B | $124.3B | +16% | 
| Net Income | $42.1B | $36.3B | +16% | 
| Diluted EPS | $2.84 | $2.40 | +19% | 
| Gross Margin | 48.2% | 46.9% | +130 bps | 
| Operating Cash Flow | $53.9B | — | All-time record | 
Source: Apple Q1 FY2026 Earnings Release
How Many iPhones Does Apple Sell?
Apple shipped 247.8 million iPhones worldwide in 2025, a 6.76% increase from 2024. iPhone revenue reached $209 billion for fiscal year 2025, accounting for 50% of total Apple revenue.
In Q1 fiscal 2026, iPhone revenue jumped to $85.3 billion from $69.1 billion the prior year, driven by demand for the iPhone 17 series launched in September 2025.

Apple Market Share by Country
Apple led the global smartphone market in Q1 2026 with 21% share, the first time it topped a first-quarter ranking, according to Counterpoint Research. Samsung held 20%, followed by Xiaomi at 12%.
Apple shipments grew 5% year over year in Q1 2026, while the broader market saw competitors decline by up to 19%.

Apple Statistics 2026 by Product Category
iPhone made up 59% of Apple’s Q1 2026 revenue. Services climbed to a record $30 billion, while iPad grew 6% to $8.6 billion. Mac revenue declined 7% to $8.4 billion as the segment faced tough year-ago comparisons.

How Many Active Apple Devices Are There?
Apple’s installed base reached 2.5 billion active devices in January 2026, up 150 million from the 2.35 billion reported a year earlier. The figure has grown by approximately 150 million devices each year since 2024.
This installed base supports Apple’s services business, where every active iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision device acts as a gateway for subscriptions.

Apple Services Statistics 2026
Services brought in $109.34 billion for fiscal year 2025, up from $96.17 billion in fiscal 2024. The segment is now Apple’s second-largest revenue source after iPhone.
Apple has crossed one billion paid subscriptions across its platforms, including first-party services and third-party app subscriptions billed through the App Store. The App Store averaged more than 850 million weekly users globally in 2025.

Apple Statistics 2026: Regional Performance
Apple posted record revenue across every geographic segment in Q1 2026. Greater China revenue grew 38% year over year, marking the strongest regional growth. The Americas remains the largest region, accounting for roughly 42% of total revenue.
India and emerging markets including the Caribbean and Latin America saw double-digit growth in 2025, helping offset earlier weakness in Greater China.
App Store Statistics 2026
Consumer spending on iOS reached $117.6 billion in 2025, up 13.6% from the previous year. Games accounted for $51.9 billion of that total, with apps contributing $64.8 billion. The App Store generated approximately $138 billion in global revenue in 2025.
About 38 billion apps were downloaded from the App Store in 2025, and lifetime downloads have surpassed 370 billion. ChatGPT was the most downloaded iOS app of 2025 with 217 million downloads.

Apple Statistics 2026: Cash and Capital Returns
Apple generated $53.9 billion from operating activities in Q1 2026, an all-time record. The company ended the quarter with $45.3 billion in cash and equivalents.
Apple returned $25 billion to shareholders through buybacks and $3.9 billion via dividends in Q1 2026 alone. The board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.26 per share, payable February 12, 2026.

Apple reported $416 billion in total revenue for fiscal year 2025, a 6.4% increase over the prior year. iPhone sales contributed roughly 50% of that total, while services brought in $109.34 billion.

Apple confirmed 2.5 billion active devices in its January 2026 earnings call, up from 2.35 billion a year earlier. The installed base added 150 million devices in 12 months.

Apple held 21% global smartphone market share in Q1 2026 according to Counterpoint Research, ranking first for the first time in any Q1. Samsung followed at 20%, with Xiaomi at 12%.
How much revenue does Apple Services generate?
Apple Services generated $109.34 billion in fiscal 2025 and a record $30 billion in Q1 fiscal 2026. The segment includes the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, Apple TV+, AppleCare, and advertising.
How many iPhones did Apple sell in 2025?
Apple shipped 247.8 million iPhones globally in 2025, a 6.76% year-over-year increase. The figure made Apple the leading smartphone seller worldwide, ahead of Samsung’s 241.2 million units.

title: SBI Q2 Results: ₹23,040 crore profit, steady growth with improved asset quality
snippet: State Bank of India reported strong Q2 FY27 results with net profit rising 25% year-on-year to ₹25,250 crore, driven by ...
content:
State Bank of India delivered a steady quarter with standalone net profit of ₹23,040 crore, up 14.3% year-on-year from ₹20,160 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. However, the headline operating performance was subdued due to treasury losses and higher operating expenses. The results exceeded analyst expectations, with Antique Stock Broking noting that adjusting for the one-off gain, PAT was ~₹17,000 crore, approximately 15% below estimates due to a ₹1,280 crore mark-to-market treasury loss compared with ₹4,300 crore gain in Q1. The exceptional growth was largely attributed to exceptional gains of ₹7,300 crore from the sale of SBI Funds Management stake, compared with ₹4,593 crore a year earlier, which significantly boosted the bank's total other income. However, ₹2,850 crore proceeds from the NSE share sale were conspicuously absent from the bank's reported profit and loss account, as per CNBC-TV18. The difference lies in accounting classification rather than any omission, with the NSE stake sale proceeds treated differently in the bank's books.
SBI's net interest income (NII) increased 14.7% year-on-year to ₹49,143 crore, beating estimates and demonstrating robust loan growth across all segments. Total advances rose 18% year-on-year, with gross advances increasing 17.8% to ₹52 lakh crore from ₹44.2 lakh crore in the year-ago quarter. As per The Hindu BusinessLine, deposits grew 12.3% to ₹62.7 lakh crore, with $10.9 billion mobilised through the bank's FCNR (B) deposit scheme. Excluding FCNR (B) deposits, overall deposit growth stood at 10.5-10.6%. The bank maintained its net interest margin (NIM) at 2.94%, expanding 7 basis points sequentially versus estimates of 2.83%, demonstrating strong liability management despite margin pressures faced by other banks. Domestic cost of deposits fell sharply to 4.84% in September 2026 from 5.13% a year ago, helping the bank maintain stable margins. Domestic net interest margin (NIM) improved 11 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 3.11%, supporting the bank's profitability metrics. According to Citi, the bank's net interest income beat expectations as domestic net interest margin rose 8 basis points to 3.11%, with the bank prioritising margins over growth. Chairman C S Setty said that the potential rate hikes will help the margin, adding that the bank expects to maintain NIM above 3%.
SBI Chairman CS Setty expressed confidence in sustaining growth momentum, announcing credit growth guidance of 14-15% and deposit growth of 10-11% for the current fiscal year. Speaking to The Times of India, Setty highlighted the bank's strong liquidity position with excess surplus liquidity of ₹3.5-4 lakh crore. "If nominal GDP growth is around 12-12.5 per cent, normally the SBI growth rate is 3 to 4 percent over that and that is where the guidance of 14 per cent to 15 per cent coming from," he stated. The bank expects corporate credit growth of around 16% year-on-year for the remainder of FY27 and maintains a corporate loan pipeline of ₹7.8 lakh crore. Setty noted that productive sectors including MSMEs and corporates will not be significantly impacted by potential rate hikes, with moderation expected only in consumption credit. The bank continues to lead in current account savings account (CASA) deposits with robust deposit growth in the retail term deposit segment at around 13-14%. However, Citi noted that loan growth of 18.2% year-on-year lagged the system, while corporate lending remained flat. Jefferies expects net interest income growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12% over FY27-FY9 and has raised its profit estimates for the period by 1-2%.
Asset quality showed remarkable improvement with GNPA ratio declining to 1.4%, down 8 basis points quarter-on-quarter from 1.52% in Q1, while NNPA ratio stood at 0.4%, down from 0.42% in the previous quarter. The Times of India reports that loan loss provisions fell 33% to ₹2,759 crore as asset quality improved significantly. The Hindu BusinessLine reports that Gross NPA stood at ₹72,529 crore and Net NPA at ₹18,546 crore on an absolute basis. The provision coverage ratio (PCR) stood at 74.43%, rising to 91.83% when accounts under collection were included. NDTV Profit reports that both GNPA and NNPA ratios were better than Street estimates of 1.45% and 0.37% respectively. The slippage ratio improved by 17 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 0.4%, while credit cost declined by 17 basis points YoY to 0.22% during the quarter. The bank's capital to risk-weighted assets ratio (CRAR) stood at 16.09% at the end of Q2 FY27, demonstrating strong capital adequacy. Chairman CS Setty emphasized that cybersecurity remains paramount importance, with the bank strengthening protocols through vulnerability assessments, patch management and API management to ensure more robust systems. Jefferies notes that the bank's asset quality remains strong, with a gross slippage ratio of 0.5% of past-year loans and a credit cost of 0.2% of average loans.
SBI shares gained 0.73% to ₹977.30 by around 1 pm on Wednesday afternoon, with the stock touching an intraday high of ₹988. Traded volume crossed 97.92 lakh shares worth ₹957 crore, reflecting active interest following last week's Q2FY27 earnings release. Sell orders dominated, accounting for 68.68% of the order book. SBI shares closed 0.95% higher at ₹978.85 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of ₹9,03,461.30 crore on Wednesday. Analyst reactions after the results have been broadly positive, though targets have diverged. CLSA retained its Outperform rating with a target of ₹1,325, citing a 2% NII beat driven by an 11-basis-point QoQ domestic NIM expansion. Citi maintained Buy at ₹1,300, highlighting resilient margins and clean asset quality. Axis Direct and Motilal Oswal both kept Buy ratings with targets of ₹1,275 and ₹1,225 respectively. Macquarie set an Outperform target at ₹1,220, while HSBC reiterated Buy at ₹1,220. However, not all were bullish - UBS and Nomura held Neutral ratings with ₹1,100 target each, flagging weaker underlying pre-provision operating profit and softer retail loan growth. Bernstein remained cautious at Market Perform with ₹1,300, noting that excluding one-offs, EPS grew only 5% YoY against the reported 13%, with RoA at 0.90% versus the reported 1.19%. The stock remains well below its 52-week high of ₹1,234.70, hit in February.

Core income grew 9.70 percent
Standalone net interest income increased 9.70 percent year over year to INR 346.20 billion in the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Standalone net profit reached INR 195.10 billion, up 4.70 percent from the same quarter a year earlier, while consolidated profit was INR 207.00 billion, the filing said.
The results were approved on October 17, 2026, and covered the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026. Net revenue reached INR 484.50 billion, compared with INR 459.00 billion in the corresponding quarter of 2025.
Deposits expanded faster than profit
End-of-period deposits rose 18.80 percent year over year to INR 33.27 trillion on September 30, 2026, while gross advances increased 16.30 percent to INR 32.20 trillion. Time deposits grew 22.80 percent, whereas current account and savings deposits rose 10.80 percent and represented 31.60 percent of total deposits.
The net interest margin was 3.16 percent on total assets in the September quarter, down from 3.26 percent in the June quarter. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 18.87 percent on September 30, 2026, leaving a substantial cushion over the stated regulatory requirement of 11.90 percent.

HDFC Bank's next major investor reference is the September quarter and half-year report approved on October 17, 2026. The results combine 4.70 percent profit growth with a 1.11 percent gross nonperforming asset ratio and 18.87 percent capital adequacy.

title: HDFC Bank Q2 net rises 5%, misses estimates
snippet: HDFC Bank posted a 5% increase in Q2 net profit to Rs 19,510 crore, missed profit estimates due to lower treasury gains, while credit growth reached 16.3% amid C-suite leadership changes.
content:
HDFC Bank’s net profit for the quarter ended September increased by nearly 5% on year to Rs 19,510 crore. The bank missed the analyst estimate of Rs 19,606 crore as per Bloomberg for the bottom line. Explaining the relatively muted profit growth despite strong business expansion, the management pointed to lower treasury gains compared with the year-ago quarter. “Normalised for the treasury trading gains, you see the year-on-year profit growth is 12.6%,” the management said.
The net interest income was up 9.7% on year to Rs 34,619 crore for the reporting quarter. Other income was also lower by 3.6% on year due to lower treasury gains. Net interest margin stood at 3.16% for the July-September quarter, lower as against 3.30% a quarter ago. Analysts had pegged the net interest margins at 3.37% for the reporting quarter.
“The margin trajectory should be upwards from the next quarter onward,” outgoing MD and CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan said in the post-earnings call on Saturday. The bank’s margins had been affected by a higher proportion of non-retail assets and liabilities, along with the impact of FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation.
While the upward interest rate trajectory should support margins, Jagdishan cautioned that the full benefit would take a few quarters to materialise as the bank gradually changes its asset mix. The management also acknowledged that margins were below its earlier expectations and indicated that recovery could take another couple of quarters.
The gross advances of the bank were up 16.3% on year to Rs 32.20 lakh crore as on September 30 and the total deposits were up 18.8% on year to Rs 33.27 lakh crore.
Within gross advances, retail book grew 11.7% on year, small and mid-market book rose 24% and the corporate and other wholesale book was up 16.4%. Retail assets grew 17% on year. This includes the FCNR leverage loans of Rs 54,800 crore, excluding which the growth would be 9.1% on year and 4.3% on quarter. The bank has adopted a cautious approach to home loan pricing amid intense competition. “We have been happy to let some of these deals go where the margin doesn’t make any sense,” Jagdishan said, adding that the bank was not necessarily competing on pricing.
He indicated that the incoming management could explore selling down or securitising part of the bank’s home loan portfolio, subject to market conditions and investor appetite. Such a strategy could allow the lender to compete more aggressively on home loan pricing while managing its balance sheet exposure.
Within deposits, the current account and savings account (CASA) deposits grew by 10.8%, with savings account deposits at Rs 7.16 lakh crore and current account deposits at Rs 3.36 lakh crore. Time deposits stood at Rs 22.76 lakh crore, an increase of 22.8% over the corresponding quarter of the previous year. CASA deposits accounted for 31.6% of total deposits as of September 30. The bank said the landed cost of its FCNR(B) deposits was between 6% and 6.25%. On relatively lower mobilisation compared with some peers, Jagdishan pointed to the bank’s limited overseas presence. “We probably did whatever we could with the kind of resources that we had,” he said, adding that expanding the bank’s overseas footprint could be part of its future strategy.
Provisions and contingencies rose by 2.1% on year and 16.8% on a sequential basis to Rs 3,574 crore in the reporting quarter. The asset quality improved during the quarter with the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio at 1.11% as against 1.17% a quarter ago and the net NPA ratio stood at 0.37% as 0.41% a quarter ago. The total capital adequacy ratio of the bank stood at 18.9%, with tier-1 capital ratio at 17.2%. Average liquidity coverage ratio stood at 113% as on September end.
Incoming MD and CEO Anup Bagchi said much of the bank’s post-merger balance sheet transformation was complete, although some work remained. “Much of it is behind us. Some more work needs to be done,” he said, adding that his immediate priority would be to engage with regulators, customers and other stakeholders before formulating his strategy.
Addressing concerns over senior management exits, Jagdishan said the bank’s operations were driven by institutional processes rather than individual personalities. “The depth in management is so large that the continuity and the ethos of the institution will be intact as well,” he said.
Dy MD Bharucha quits
Mumbai: HDFC Bank on Saturday said its Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha has sought to step down from the bank with effect from the close of business hours on December 31, marking the end of an association spanning more than three decades. The bank’s Governance, Nomination and Remuneration Committee and board of directors have accepted his request, which will be forwarded to RBI for approval. Bharucha’s departure comes amid a leadership transition at the country’s largest private sector lender, with MD and CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan set to retire later this month and Anup Bagchi scheduled to take charge on October 27.
Separately, the board approved the reappointment of former RBI Executive Director Lily Vadera as an independent director for three years, from November 26, subject to shareholder approval.

title: Net interest income - Latest net interest income , Information & Updates - BFSI -ET BFSI
snippet: ETBFSI.com brings latest net interest income news, views and updates from all top sources for the Indian BFSI industry.
content:
Banks could see further acceleration in net interest income growth from current levels, even if headline loan growth moderates as their portfolios gradually move away from corporate lending.
While asset quality has improved, several banks have chosen not to lower their credit cost guidance despite reporting provisions below guidance, indicating that the current benefit may not be sustained as ECL provisioning is introduced.
Bajaj Finance announced a strong first-quarter profit exceeding expectations. Loan growth accelerated, contributing significantly to the company's financial performance. Retail credit demand remained robust, supporting asset management growth. The lender's net interest income saw a substantial year-on-year increase. Improved asset quality was noted with a lower gross non-performing asset ratio.
Karnataka Bank reported a 43% year-on-year rise in Q1 net profit to Rs 419 crore, driven by stronger business growth, improved asset quality and lower provisions. Net interest income, operating profit and margins increased, while advances and deposits posted healthy year-on-year growth.
Tamilnad Mercantile Bank reported a 35% year-on-year rise in June quarter net profit to Rs 412 crore, driven by higher income and net interest income. The lender also posted improved margins, stronger asset quality and robust growth in advances and deposits.
Bank of Baroda's June-quarter profit fell 72% due to a Rs 5,680 crore one-off settlement, despite strong loan growth and stable asset quality. Excluding the exceptional item, profit rose, supported by higher net interest income and healthy retail lending.
The fund acquired an additional 1.46 crore shares through the open market, taking its total holding to 5.16 per cent of the bank's paid-up equity capital.
Federal Bank reported a 37% net profit increase for Q1FY27. Net interest income rose significantly, driven by advances growth. Operating profit also saw a substantial expansion during this period. Total deposits and gross advances experienced healthy year-on-year growth. The bank received approval to raise substantial funds for future expansion.
Shalibhadra Finance is set for major expansion. The company aims to more than double its loan book by FY29. This growth will be fueled by new products like Micro LAP and home loans. Geographic expansion into new states is also planned. Technology investments will enhance efficiency. Shalibhadra Finance is positioning itself for significant growth in the retail finance sector.
Shalibhadra Finance has announced a strong financial performance. The non-banking finance company saw its profit after tax climb by 15.5 per cent to Rs 5.13 crore for the quarter ending March 2026. For the full fiscal year 2025-26, profit after tax grew by 21.67 per cent. Assets under management also saw a significant increase.
Poonawalla Fincorp announced a significant profit jump for the March quarter. Profit after tax surged to Rs 255 crore, a more than four-fold increase from the previous year. Total income also saw a substantial rise. The company's assets under management reached Rs 60,348 crore. A recent capital raise provides ample room for future expansion.
Growth momentum has strengthened, with nearly 50% of FY26 incremental loan growth coming in the fourth quarter and the secured portfolio mix improving to around 56%.

title: HDFC Bank’s Q2FY27 net profit edges up 4.7%; asset quality improves
snippet: Oct 17, 2026 · HDFC Bank reports a 4.7% rise in Q2FY27 net profit to ₹19,509.3 crore, with improved asset quality and gross NPA ratio dropping to 1.11%. Discover key financial highlights, including a 9.7% growth in net interest income and robust retail advances.
content:
HDFC Bank’s Q2FY27 net profit edges up 4.7%; asset quality improves
ADVERTISEMENT
HDFC Bank on Saturday reported a standalone net profit of ₹19,509.3 crore for the September-ended quarter (Q2FY27), up 4.7% from a year earlier. Its top line or net interest income (NII) rose 9.7% year-on-year to ₹34,619.2 crore, the bank said.
This is the last quarterly financial earnings data to be announced under the leadership of Sashidhar Jagdishan, the managing director & CEO, whose term ends on October 26, 2026. The Reserve Bank of India has already approved the appointment of Anup Bagchi, an ICICI Group veteran, who was most recently serving as the MD & CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance. He will be taking charge from October 27, 2026.
HDFC Bank’s net interest margin was at 3.16% on total assets, and 3.32% based on interest earning assets. NIM’s for the bank have been on the decline since the bank’s merger with HDFC in 2023.
Other income (non-interest revenue) for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was ₹13,831 crore.
HDFC Bank’s gross NPA ratio improved to 1.11% for the September-ended quarter, from 1.24% a year earlier. The retail advances for the bank were at 1.08%. Gross advances for the bank came in at ₹32.19 lakh crore.
The cost-to-income ratio for the quarter was 39.1%. The Bank's average deposits were ₹31.66 lakh crore for the September 2026 quarter, a growth of 16.8% for the corresponding period a year earlier.
Provisions and contingencies stood at ₹3,570 crore during the quarter.
CASA deposits grew by 10.8% with savings account deposits, accounting for 3.16% of total deposits.
The total balance sheet size of the bank was at ₹45.77 lakh crore as of the September-ended quarter, as against ₹40,03 lakh crore a year earlier.
As far as the retail book is concerned, the book grew by 11.1% over the previous year, at ₹17.37 lakh crore, of which personal loans contributed ₹9.2 lakh crore. Small and mid-market loans were at ₹7.06 lakh crore.
Analysts have said that after the mega-merger with HDFC, HDFC Bank — which was seen as a low-margin, low-cost lender — is unlikely to surge sharply, in a few quarters. But it is expected to keep inching up gradually—as its top management said at the August AGM—which could see its RoE improve.

title: HDFC Bank Q2 Results: Margins at record low; Treasury income drops 67% - CNBC TV18
snippet: Oct 17, 2026 · HDFC Bank reported a Q2 net profit of ₹19,510 crore, rising 4.7% to meet estimates. Core NII grew 9.7%, asset quality improved with gross NPA at 1.11%, and deposits rose 18.8%, ahead of a leadership transition.
content:
HDFC Bank Q2 Results: Margins at record low; Treasury income drops 67%
- Published OnOct 17, 2026 | 14:08 IST
- Last Updated OnOct 17, 2026 | 15:56 IST
HDFC Bank reported a Q2 net profit of ₹19,510 crore, rising 4.7% to meet estimates. Core NII grew 9.7%, asset quality improved with gross NPA at 1.11%, and deposits rose 18.8%, ahead of a leadership transition.
HDFC Bank, India's largest private sector lender, reported September quarter results on Saturday, October 17, which were in-line with analyst expectations.
Net Interest Income (NII) or the bank's core income grew 9.7% in Q2FY26 to ₹34,620 crore from ₹31,552 last year. A CNBC-TV18 poll had estimated an NII of ₹34,861 crore.
Net profit for the September quarter stood at ₹19,510 crore, up 4.7% from from ₹18,641 crore in Q2FY26. The bank's bottom line stood in line with the CNBC-TV18 poll estimate of ₹19,567 crore.
HDFC Bank's net interest margin (NIM) declined to 3.16% in the September quarter, its lowest on record, compared with 3.26% in the June quarter.
The bank's treasury trading income declined 67.4% year-on-year to ₹780 crore, compared with ₹2,390 crore in Q2FY26.. Excluding treasury trading gains, HDFC Bank's net profit grew 12.6% year-on-year, compared with reported growth of 4.7%.
The bank's cost-to-income ratio stood at 39.1% during the quarter. Its total credit cost ratio was 0.44%.
Provisions stood at ₹3,574 crore, compared with ₹3,010 crore in the previous quarter and ₹3,501 crore in the year-ago quarter.
HDFC Bank's asset quality remained stable during the September quarter, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) in absolute terms at ₹35,810 crore, compared with ₹35,846 crore in June.
Net non-performing assets (NNPA) stood at ₹11,851 crore, against ₹12,357 crore in the previous quarter. In percentage terms, the gross NPA ratio stood at 1.11%, while the net NPA ratio was 0.37%, compared with 1.17% and 0.41%, respectively, in the June quarter. The Street had estimated the gross NPA ratio at 1.17% for the September quarter.
HDFC Bank's gross NPA ratio, excluding agriculture, stood at 0.87% in the September quarter, compared with 0.91% in the previous quarter and 0.99% in the year-ago period.
The bank's capital adequacy ratio stood at 18.9%, compared with 20% in the corresponding quarter last year.
As per its provisional business update for the September quarter, HDFC Bank's gross advances grew 16.3% year-on-year to ₹32.19 lakh crore. On a sequential basis, advances increased by 5.2%.
The bank's average advances under management, adjusted for inter-bank participation certificates, bills rediscounted, securitisation and assignment, grew 14% year-on-year to ₹31.87 lakh crore. The period-end figure stood at ₹33.07 lakh crore, a growth of 15.3% from the same quarter last year.
Total deposits at HDFC Bank stood at ₹33.27 lakh crore at the end of September, up 18.8% from the year-ago period. On a sequential basis, deposits grew 4.9%, slower than the 5.2% sequential growth in gross advances.
Within deposits, current account and savings account (CASA) deposits grew 10.8% year-on-year to ₹10.52 lakh crore. On a sequential basis, CASA deposits increased by 2.6%. Term deposits rose 22.8% year-on-year and 6.1% quarter-on-quarter to ₹22.75 lakh crore.
In its business update, HDFC Bank also disclosed that it had mobilised $11.5 billion worth of FCNR(B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India's swap window. The bank's overseas branches extended loan facilities aggregating to $5.7 billion against these deposits. It had also issued $2.5 billion worth of US dollar-denominated senior unsecured bonds.
The results come amid investor focus on the bank's leadership transition, following the appointment of Anup Bagchi as the next managing director and chief executive officer. Bagchi is set to take charge after Sashidhar Jagdishan's term ends on October 26.
“A 10–12 basis point reduction in the margin was what we were expecting. It has come in, and it is exactly there,” Dharmesh Kant of Chola Securities said.
Kant said HDFC Bank's margins could remain at current levels if the lender does not return to stronger retail loan growth. He noted that the bank's return on assets (RoA) was still around 1.7–1.75% based on first-half numbers, below the 2% level it was previously known for. “A re-rating will take time. I don't think it will happen immediately,” he said.
“The initial numbers and the first print probably look very much in line with estimates,” Mayuresh Joshi, Director of Research at Marketsmith India, said.
Joshi said the marginal improvement in asset quality and the deployment of FCNR(B) deposits over the next few months could support the bank's performance over the coming quarters. He added that the management transition and the strategic decisions that follow could help set the path for structural growth.
Watch accompanying video for full conversation.
Bernstein on HDFC Bank Q2 Earnings
Bernstein said HDFC Bank's weak earnings growth trend continued in the September quarter, with healthy balance-sheet growth and resilient asset quality offset by weaker treasury income and margin pressure.
“Healthy NII growth, subdued non-interest income growth, continued opex discipline and higher provisioning resulted in another quarter of weak earnings growth,” the brokerage said.
Bernstein noted that loan growth continued to be led by the corporate and mid-market segments, which grew 16% and 24% year-on-year, respectively, while retail loan growth remained relatively subdued at 12%. Net interest income grew 10% year-on-year, supported by 16% loan growth and 19% deposit growth.
The brokerage added that operating expense growth remained contained at 6% year-on-year, while credit costs increased 17% sequentially. Return on assets moderated by around 4 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 1.8%.
Shares of HDFC Bank ended 0.3% higher at ₹728.85 on Friday, ahead of the results announcement. The stock has declined nearly 27% so far in 2026.

What are financial ratios and why are they important?
What does gross profit margin indicate?
It measures the efficiency of production. A higher margin means the company retains more per unit of sales.
How is net profit margin different from operating margin?
Net profit margin includes all expenses, including tax and interest. Operating margin only considers income from operations (EBIT).
What is earnings per share (EPS)?
It shows how much profit is earned per share — a key metric for investors.
Why is return on equity (ROE) important?
ROE shows how efficiently a company uses shareholders' funds.
What does the current ratio show?
It measures short-term liquidity. A ratio greater than 1 means the firm can meet its short-term obligations.
What does return on assets (ROA) measure?
ROA indicates how efficiently assets generate profit.
What is the operating cash flow ratio?
It assesses whether operating cash flows can cover short-term liabilities.
What does the cash flow margin show?
It reflects how effectively sales are converted into actual cash.
How do financial ratios help investors?
They provide a quick way to evaluate company performance, financial health, and risk, and to compare across peers or industry benchmarks.

title: HDFC Bank Q2 results: Net profit rises 4.7% to Rs 19,510 crore, broadly meets estimates; asset quality improves- Moneycontrol.com
snippet: Oct 17, 2026 · HDFC Bank Q2 FY27 Financial Results: Net profit rose 4.7 percent to Rs 19,510 crore, broadly meeting estimates, while NII grew 9.7 percent. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA declining to 1.11 ...
content:
HDFC Bank on Saturday reported a 4.7 percent year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 19,510 crore for the second quarter of FY27, broadly meeting market expectations. The private sector lender's net interest income (NII) rose 9.7 percent to Rs 34,619.2 crore, while asset quality improved both sequentially and on a year-on-year basis.
A CNBC TV18 poll had projected a 5 percent increase in net profit to Rs 19,567 crore and a 10 percent rise in NII to Rs 34,861 crore. Both reported figures were within 1 percent of the estimates.
HDFC Bank's net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.16 percent on total assets, down from 3.26 percent in the previous quarter. The NIM on interest-earning assets during the July-September quarter was at 3.32 percent.
Provisions and contingencies rose 18.7 percent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 3,574 crore from Rs 3,010 crore in the June quarter. On a year-on-year basis, provisions increased 2.1 percent from Rs 3,501 crore.
HDFC Bank's gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio improved to 1.11 percent as of September 30, 2026, from 1.17 percent in the preceding quarter and 1.24 percent a year earlier. Excluding non-performing assets in the agricultural segment, the GNPA ratio stood at 0.87 percent, compared with 0.91 percent in June 2026 and 0.99 percent in September 2025.
Gross non-performing assets (NPAs) stood at Rs 35,810 crore at the end of September, marginally lower than Rs 35,846 crore in the preceding quarter. Net NPAs declined 4.1 percent sequentially to Rs 11,851 crore from Rs 12,357 crore.
The net NPA ratio stood at 0.37 percent at the end of the September quarter.
The bank's gross advances rose 16.3 percent year-on-year to Rs 32,19,500 crore as of September 30, 2026, while advances under management grew 15.3 percent.
Retail loans increased 11.7 percent, small and mid-market enterprise loans grew 23.5 percent, and corporate and other wholesale loans expanded 16.4 percent.
Average advances under management stood at Rs 31,87,200 crore during the quarter, up 14.1 percent year-on-year and 4.9 percent sequentially.
Total deposits increased 18.8 percent year-on-year to Rs 33,27,400 crore at the end of September. Average deposits rose 16.8 percent to Rs 31,66,400 crore, registering sequential growth of 5.1 percent.
CASA deposits grew 10.8 percent year-on-year, accounting for 31.6 percent of total deposits. Time deposits increased 22.8 percent.
HDFC Bank's capital adequacy ratio under Basel III stood at 18.9 percent as of September 30, 2026, compared with 20 percent a year earlier and a regulatory requirement of 11.9 percent. The Tier 1 capital adequacy ratio stood at 17.2 percent, while the Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio was 17.1 percent.
The bank reported net revenue of Rs 48,450 crore for the quarter, compared with Rs 45,900 crore a year earlier. Other income stood at Rs 13,830 crore, including fees and commissions of Rs 9,690 crore. Treasury trading gains declined to Rs 780 crore from Rs 2,390 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Operating expenses increased to Rs 18,970 crore from Rs 17,980 crore a year earlier, while the cost-to-income ratio stood at 39.1 percent. The bank said net profit excluding treasury trading gains grew approximately 12.6 percent year-on-year.
The total credit cost ratio was 0.44 percent.
HDFC Bank shares closed 0.28 percent higher at Rs 728.85 on Friday, ahead of the results announcement. The stock has declined 26.5 percent so far in 2026, compared with an 11.5 percent fall in the Nifty 50. The bank's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs 11.24 lakh crore.
