title: HDFC Bank Q2 net profit rises 4.7% to ₹19,510 crore as NII grows
snippet: Oct 16, 2026 · Listen to This Article India’s largest private sector lender, HDFC Bank, on Saturday reported a 4.7 per cent year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹19,510 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), as a decline in other income and higher operating expenses and provisions partly offset growth in core interest income.
content:
HDFC Bank Q2 net profit rises 4.7% to ₹19,510 crore as NII grows
Net interest income rose 9.7 per cent to ₹34,620 crore and deposits grew 18.8 per cent, while lower treasury gains and higher expenses capped profit growth
Listen to This Article
India’s largest private sector lender, HDFC Bank, on Saturday reported a 4.7 per cent year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹19,510 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), as a decline in other income and higher operating expenses and provisions partly offset growth in core interest income.
 
Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, rose 9.7 per cent year-on-year to ₹34,620 crore, supported by 16.3 per cent growth in gross advances.
 
Other income declined 3.6 per cent year-on-year to ₹13,830 crore, primarily reflecting a sharp fall in treasury trading gains. However, it rose nearly 8 per cent sequentially.
Fees and commissions, the largest component of other income, increased to ₹9,690 crore from ₹8,840 crore a year earlier.
 
Foreign exchange and derivatives revenue declined marginally to ₹1,550 crore from ₹1,590 crore, while treasury trading gains fell sharply to ₹780 crore from ₹2,390 crore.
Also Read
Miscellaneous income, including recoveries and dividends, rose to ₹1,810 crore from ₹1,530 crore.
 
Net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.16 per cent of total assets and 3.32 per cent of interest-earning assets.
 
Operating expenses increased to ₹18,970 crore from ₹17,980 crore in the corresponding quarter a year earlier.
 
The cost-to-income ratio stood at 39.1 per cent.
 
Provisions and contingencies for the quarter amounted to ₹3,570 crore, while the total credit cost ratio stood at 0.44 per cent.
The bank’s gross advances stood at ₹32.2 trillion as of September 30, 2026, registering 16.3 per cent growth over a year earlier.
 
Average advances under management, adjusted for transfers through inter-bank participation certificates, bills rediscounted and securitisation or assignment, rose 14.1 per cent year-on-year to ₹31.87 trillion. They were up 4.9 per cent sequentially.
 
Retail loans grew 11.7 per cent year-on-year, while loans to small and mid-market enterprises increased 23.5 per cent.
 
Corporate and other wholesale loans rose 16.4 per cent. Overseas advances accounted for 3.3 per cent of total advances.
 
Total end-of-period deposits increased 18.8 per cent year-on-year to ₹33.27 trillion as of September 30, 2026.
Within this, time deposits rose 22.8 per cent to ₹22.76 trillion, while current account and savings account (CASA) deposits grew 10.8 per cent.
 
Savings account deposits stood at ₹7.16 trillion and current account deposits at ₹3.36 trillion.
 
CASA deposits accounted for 31.6 per cent of total deposits as of September 30, 2026.
 
The bank’s total balance sheet size increased to ₹45.78 trillion as of September 30, 2026, from ₹40.03 trillion a year earlier.
 
The bank’s gross non-performing assets (GNPA) ratio improved to 1.11 per cent of gross advances as of September 30, 2026, from 1.17 per cent in the June quarter and 1.24 per cent a year earlier.
Excluding non-performing assets in the agricultural segment, the GNPA ratio stood at 0.87 per cent, compared with 0.91 per cent in the June quarter and 0.99 per cent a year earlier.
 
Net non-performing assets stood at 0.37 per cent of net advances as of September 30, 2026. 
“I think the topline has been extremely healthy. We have seen strong underlying business momentum, particularly in the retail and MSME segments, which are moving in the right direction. The margin trajectory should turn upwards from the next quarter onwards. Our asset quality also continues to be extremely strong, which has been our USP through various business cycles, and we believe this will remain so for a long time”, said Sashidhar Jagdishan, MD&CEO, HDFC Bank.  
On a consolidated basis, the bank reported net revenue of ₹78,690 crore and net profit of ₹20,700 crore for Q2FY27.
 
Consolidated net profit for the first half of FY27 stood at ₹39,940 crore. 
Seperately, Jagdishan also introduced the MD&CEO designate of the bank Anup Bagchi, who will succeed Jagdishan on October 27. “We welcome Anup with open arms. I believe he will bring a fresh perspective, and we wish him all the very best in his tenure as the CEO of HDFC Bank,” he said. 
 
In his opening remarks, Bagchi said: “I am very grateful to the board for the trust it has placed in me to lead the bank. I look forward to working with the board, the chairman and the leadership team. I would also like to thank Shashi for his leadership over the past six years. He has steered the bank through the post-pandemic period, overseen the landmark merger and helped scale up the branch network and strengthen the bank’s core technology capabilities. Accomplishing all of this in six years has been a significant undertaking.
Bagchi also thanked Kaizad Bharucha, deputy MD, HDFC Bank for his contribution as he has decided to exit the bank at the end of December this year. 
 
“I would also like to thank Kaizad. One of the most distinguishing strengths of HDFC Bank, and the HDFC group more broadly, has been its robust credit quality across cycles and regimes. Since the bank was established in 1995, the country and its banking institutions have gone through several phases of credit cycles. The fact that the institution has maintained such strong credit quality is a testament to Kaizad and the deeply committed team he has helped build”, Bagchi said. 
“The post-merger balance sheet and the broader transformation are still works in progress, but I believe much of that journey is behind us. There is still work to be done, and I am grateful to the board for giving me this opportunity. We will work together with the team to ensure that the bank continues to move from strength to strength”, Bagchi said.

title: Tesla vs. Ford: Which Stock Has an Edge After Q3 Earnings?
snippet: TSLA looks better positioned after Q3 earnings, backed by improving vehicle demand, margins and...
content:
Tesla TSLA and Ford F both topped Wall Street's third-quarter 2026 EPS estimates, but what investors took away from the two reports was quite different. Tesla tackled its biggest overhang by cutting its 2026 capital expenditure plan from $25 billion to $20 billion. Ford tightened its 2026 adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.5 billion-$11 billion, from $10 billion-$11 billion earlier, and said 2027 earnings should be roughly in line with this year's.
Over the past month, Tesla shares have gained 14% while Ford has lost 1%. With third-quarter results now behind us, which stock is better positioned from here?
Image Source: Zacks Investment Research
The Case for Tesla
Tesla's case rests on improving vehicle demand, healthier auto and energy margins and an AI roadmap with measurable milestones, even as high R&D spending weighs on operating profit.
Tesla's deliveries and order backlog show demand holding up well. The company delivered 486,532 vehicles in its latest reported quarter, its second straight quarter above 480,000 units, and its passenger vehicle order backlog is the highest in four years. Management says demand is running well ahead of production, largely helped by rising FSD adoption. More than 75% of new North American deliveries included a paid FSD subscription at delivery. Recently, Latvia approved FSD, making it the 10th EU country to do so, according to Teslarati.
Gross margins are following volume. Automotive gross margin rose to 18.5% from 17% a year earlier. Energy storage deployments reached 13.7 GWh, up 10% year over year, while energy gross margin climbed to 33.1% from 20.4% in the second quarter of 2026. With CEO Elon Musk saying Megapack supply for 2027 is almost sold out, this business has strong forward visibility.
The AI story now has progress to show. Tesla began deploying Cybercabs in Austin in September 2026, and Musk says the fleet there has grown tenfold in roughly a month. Cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles rose eightfold sequentially to nearly 2 million. Management expects Robotaxi to contribute more meaningfully to revenues from next year.
The weak spot is operating profit, which contracted as R&D costs rose. It is expected to keep declining year over year in the coming quarters as Tesla funds its next growth cycle, and supply chain challenges persist. Still, the pressure is investment-led rather than demand-led. With strong demand, recovering gross margins, a return to positive free cash flow and tangible AI milestones, the narrative is getting stronger.
Tesla, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Tesla, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Tesla, Inc. Quote
The Case for Ford
Ford's case rests on long-term franchise strength, but the near-term numbers are under pressure across all three of its segments.
The foundation is solid. Ford leads in trucks and SUVs, is expanding Super Duty capacity and is growing its software and parts businesses. Hybrid demand, an affordable EV platform and Ford Energy add runway, but these are long-term supports that do little for the near term.
The latest quarterly results showed the strain. At Ford Blue, wholesale units, revenues, EBIT and EBIT margin all declined. Discontinued models and disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict cut sales, and higher commodity costs weighed on profitability.
Ford Pro, a key earnings contributor, also saw margins slip. Third-quarter EBIT fell 16% year over year to $1.7 billion, and EBIT margin contracted to 9.4% from 11.4%. Management trimmed its full-year Ford Pro EBIT outlook to about $7 billion from $7-$7.5 billion earlier.
Ford Model e unit remains the biggest drag, with a $1.1 billion third-quarter EBIT loss, though $352 million narrower than a year ago. Revenues fell as the F-150 Lightning ended and Mach-E output dropped. Ford expects about $4 billion in 2026 losses, and higher 2027 spending on the Universal EV platform and Ford Energy pushes meaningful improvement to 2028.
Costs are the other worry. Commodity headwinds are now expected to approach $2.5 billion in 2026, about $500 million more than the earlier guidance, and higher fuel prices are lifting freight and energy costs. Ford expects U.S. industry pricing to rise about 100 basis points, but sustained inflation could absorb that benefit. Tariff uncertainty adds to the risk, and management sees about $2 billion of combined commodity, memory and logistics headwinds in 2027, which will require further efficiency gains to protect earnings.
Ford Motor Company Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Ford Motor Company price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Ford Motor Company Quote
Our Take: TSLA Has an Upper Hand Now
Tesla's profit pressure comes from investing in growth but Ford's comes from forces it can't fully control. Tesla is spending more on R&D to build robotaxi and AI revenue streams, and it has already trimmed capex to protect cash flow. Ford's pressure comes from outside its control, including commodities, tariffs and a loss-making EV unit that will not turn around before 2028.
Tesla's demand, backlog and energy visibility suggest earnings growth next year. Ford is guiding to flat 2027 earnings, with fresh cost headwinds still to absorb.
Momentum in the business is building at Tesla, while Ford's near-term stays clouded by cost pressure and EV losses. As such, Tesla looks better placed from here.

title: Rivian Bets on R2 Margins as Volkswagen’s $1 Billion Loan Buys Time
snippet: Key TakeawaysRivian delivered a record 19,248 vehicles in the third quarter, up 46% and ahead of...
content:
Key Takeaways
-       Rivian delivered a record 19,248 vehicles in the third quarter, up 46% and ahead of estimates.
-       Automotive gross profit was still negative $36 million in the second quarter, while software and services carried margins.
-       Rivian no longer expects positive adjusted EBITDA in 2027 as autonomy spending rises.
-       The October 29 report will show whether automotive gross profit is moving toward positive.
Rivian Automotive (RIVN:NASDAQ) finally has the volume story it promised. The stock has not followed.
Rivian delivered a record 19,248 vehicles in the third quarter, up 46% from a year earlier and ahead of the roughly 18,000 analysts expected. Shares still closed at $12 on October 27, down 28.3% over three months and just above the 52-week low of $11.
The market's logic is simple. Volume only helps if each R2 eventually makes money, and Rivian has made 2027 profitability harder to see.
Thursday's third-quarter report is where those two threads meet.
The R2 ramp shows up
The third quarter was the first full quarter of R2 deliveries, which began in June. The jump was immediate.
-       Deliveries rose 58% from the second quarter's 12,194.
-       Production reached 19,751 at the Normal, Illinois plant.
-       Full-year guidance of 65,000 to 70,000 deliveries held.
Hitting the low end requires at least 23,193 fourth-quarter deliveries, a 20.5% sequential increase. Rivian built about 500 more vehicles than it delivered, which gives it a small cushion.
Scale still looks tiny next to Tesla (TSLA:NASDAQ), which delivered 486,532 vehicles in the same quarter.
Analysts model third-quarter revenue near $2 billion, up about 30%:
Software is carrying the margin
Second-quarter revenue rose 27% to $1.66 billion. Consolidated gross profit reached $179 million, a $385 million improvement from a year earlier.
Look closer, though. Automotive gross profit was still negative $36 million, while software and services revenue rose 37% to $515 million, largely through the Volkswagen Group (VOW3) joint venture.
Line up the quarters and the swing is hard to miss.
CFO Claire McDonough, who departs at the end of October, told Reuters in April that the R2 should cost less than half as much as the R1 to build once output reaches a higher run rate in 2027. She also expected Rivian to exit 2026 with positive automotive gross margins. That target matters more than any delivery number this year.

title: Rivian Automotive Inc (RIVN) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: R
snippet: Consolidated Revenue: $2.155 billion, up 38% year-over-year.Consolidated Gross Profit: $176 million,...
content:
- Consolidated Revenue: $2.155 billion, up 38% year-over-year.
- Consolidated Gross Profit: $176 million, with an 8% gross profit margin; included $166 million of depreciation and amortization and $28 million of stock-based compensation expense.
- Adjusted EBITDA Loss: $435 million for Q3.
- Production: 19,751 vehicles produced at the Normal, Illinois plant.
- Deliveries: 19,248 vehicles delivered; R2 became the best-selling vehicle by volume.
- Automotive Revenue: $1.55 billion, up 36% year-over-year, driven by a 46% increase in vehicle deliveries and $81 million of regulatory credits.
- Automotive Gross Profit (Loss): Loss of $80 million, a $50 million improvement versus the prior-year loss of $130 million.
- R2 Ramp Cost: Approximately $120 million in incremental cost of revenue due to the R2 production ramp.
- Software and Services Revenue: $605 million, up 45% year-over-year; $354 million (~60%) attributable to the Volkswagen Group joint venture.
- Software and Services Gross Profit: $256 million at a 42% margin.
- Cash and Liquidity: Approximately $5.5 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments at quarter end.
- Volkswagen Term Loan: $1 billion, 10-year facility funded October 7 at a fixed 6% interest rate.
- JV Capital Commitments: $5.3 billion of $5.8 billion received to date; remaining $460 million expected in late 2027.
- Uber Investment: Next milestone expected by year-end to unlock an additional $250 million equity investment.
- Total Available Liquidity: Approximately $13 billion including current liquidity and targeted future capital from Uber, Volkswagen, and the DOE loan.
- Full-Year Delivery Guidance: Raised to 67,000–70,000 units from 65,000–70,000 units.
- Full-Year Adjusted EBITDA Guidance: Loss of $1.85 billion to $1.75 billion, a $100 million improvement at the midpoint.
- 2026 CapEx Guidance: Lowered by $300 million at the midpoint to a range of $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion.
Release Date: October 29, 2026
For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.
Positive Points
- Rivian Automotive Inc RIVN achieved record production and deliveries in Q3 2026, with R2 becoming the best-selling vehicle by volume, outselling R1 and EDV.
- Consolidated revenue increased 38% year-over-year to $2.155 billion, driven by a 46% increase in vehicle deliveries and $81 million in regulatory credits.
- Software and services segment revenue grew 45% year-over-year to $605 million, with a 42% gross margin, reflecting strong performance in vehicle electrical architecture and Autonomy Plus.
- Rivian Automotive Inc (RIVN) improved full-year delivery guidance to 67,000-70,000 units and expects a positive automotive gross margin exit rate for 2026, driven by R2 ramp.
- The company has a strong liquidity position with $5.5 billion in cash and short-term investments, plus additional capital commitments from Volkswagen and Uber, totaling approximately $13 billion in available liquidity.
Negative Points
- Adjusted EBITDA losses were $435 million in Q3 2026, and full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA losses are expected to be between $1.85 billion and $1.75 billion.
- Automotive gross profit loss was $80 million, impacted by $120 million in incremental costs related to the R2 production ramp and rising commodity and memory costs.
- Rivian Automotive Inc (RIVN) faces supply chain challenges, including ramping up new suppliers and managing increased costs for core components like memory and steel.
- R&D expenses are expected to grow significantly in 2027, driven by strategic investments in autonomy software and hardware, which may pressure near-term profitability.
- The company expects a meaningful year-over-year step up in capital expenditures in 2027 for the Georgia manufacturing facility, which could strain cash flow despite current liquidity.
Q & A Highlights
Q: How leverageable is Rivian's autonomy platform to commercial vehicles over time? 
A: CEO RJ Scaringe said the autonomy platform is built around the "large driving model," a foundation model adaptable to different vehicle form factors, including R1, R2 and commercial vehicles. He noted applications across the consumer business (point-to-point), robotaxi (2028 Uber launch) and the commercial VANS program.
Q: Does the expected positive automotive gross margin exit rate mean a full quarter of positive margins or just a December run rate? 
A: VP of Finance Derek Mulvey clarified that Rivian intends to exit the quarter at an automotive gross profit, so investors should not expect a full quarter of positive margins, but it sets the company up well as R2 ramps through 2027.
Q: What is R2's contribution margin before launch inefficiencies and fixed cost absorption, to gauge a mature gross margin? 
A: Derek Mulvey said the $120 million in incremental cost of revenue reflects conversion costs and depreciation below a full two-shift operation, plus expedited freight and other costs expected to wind off. He noted a roughly $12,000 per unit step down in cost of goods sold per unit delivered, and that total automotive gross profit excluding regulatory credits was positive on a cash basis in the quarter.
Q: With inflation in memory, PCB, steel and copper since R2 pricing was announced, how is Rivian offsetting costs to maintain target margins? 
A: CEO RJ Scaringe said the engineering team is pursuing plant operating improvements, packaging and logistics efficiencies, and supplier-level cost optimizations such as part consolidation or elimination through redesign—without impacting vehicle performance—to deliver trims from $45,000 to about $57,000.
Q: What are the key factors determining the pace of R2 delivery growth in Q4 and 2027—converting demo drives or ramping supply chain and manufacturing? 
A: RJ Scaringe emphasized that ramping the supply base is as critical as the plant, noting Rivian reduced supply chain complexity to a smaller set of Tier 1 suppliers and can only ramp as fast as its slowest supplier. COO Javier Varela added that dedicated teams are supporting suppliers, including their tier two and tier three networks.
Q: How impactful was Autonomy Plus in the 45% year-over-year software and services growth, and is it a key purchase reason for buyers? 
A: RJ Scaringe said Autonomy Plus take rates have exceeded expectations, with universal hands-free driving on millions of miles of roads. He said the upcoming point-to-point capability—matching Tesla's FSD as the only other such product—should create new demand and become a core purchase criterion.
Q: What is driving the EDV record with Amazon, and what is the potential with other commercial customers? 
A: RJ Scaringe said Amazon has significantly stepped up demand this year due to real structural cost advantages from the EDV platform, and Rivian continues discussions with other commercial operators looking to drive efficiency into their businesses.
Q: How is the Volkswagen joint venture progressing, and could the technology expand to other automakers? 
A: RJ Scaringe said the JV's first output is Volkswagen's roughly €20,000 ID1 EV launching next year in Europe, which he called a "billboard" for the technology's capability against European and Chinese competitors. He said the technology has applications beyond Rivian and the existing JV, though focus remains on Rivian and VW programs.
Q: What does Rivian need to see from the autonomy early access program before a broader 2027 release of point-to-point? 
A: RJ Scaringe said the invitation-only program, starting later this year, is designed to gather rich, diverse feedback from customers across different driving environments and geographies—on functionality, interface and UI—to set up a full release to all Autonomy Plus subscribers in 2027.
Q: What is Rivian seeing in AI compute pricing and capacity, and how will R&D trend? 
A: Derek Mulvey said Rivian is seeing some increased pricing for leased compute. He expects low double-digit R&D growth from Q3 to Q4 2026 and more significant R&D growth in 2027 than 2026, driven by autonomy software, autonomy hardware and vehicle technologies.
Q: What is driving the $300 million reduction in 2026 capital expenditure guidance? 
A: Derek Mulvey attributed the cut to timing shifts in spend related to the Georgia facility, where large equipment purchases and contracts make spending lumpy and can shift between quarters by a few weeks. He said 2027 CapEx will step up meaningfully as Georgia construction ramps.
Q: What drove the decision to keep the LiDAR-equipped R2 variant in an employee program this year rather than consumer availability? 
A: RJ Scaringe said the next hardware generation—with Rivian's RAP1 processor (two units for 1,600 TOPS) plus camera, radar and LiDAR—is going through an employee validation program late this year and will be available in 2027. Meanwhile, the large driving model will deploy across all R2 vehicles and 2025+ R1s, enabling point-to-point on those vehicles.
Q: How are test-drive-to-order conversion rates trending versus R1, given the surge in demo drives? 
A: RJ Scaringe said conversion for the premium Launch Edition R2 has exceeded expectations despite being the most expensive R2 trim, and test drives stepped up significantly with R2 availability. He said Rivian is excited about additional trims coming in the months ahead.
Q: How is Rivian positioning R1 pricing over time relative to R2? 
A: RJ Scaringe said Rivian intentionally moved R1 upmarket by removing the standard trim, and expects R1 average selling prices to rise. R1 is positioned as the flagship—over 1,000 horsepower in quad-motor form, highly capable on- and off-road—and is not intended to be a high-volume, lower-priced product.

title: Zero To Sixty: Fort Worth Gets Tesla Robotaxi While UBS Upgrades Rivian And Citigroup Shuffles EV Holdings
snippet: Tesla expanded unsupervised Robotaxi service to Fort Worth this week while UBS upgraded Rivian and...
content:
-       Tesla launched unsupervised Robotaxi rides in Fort Worth this week across an estimated 143-square-mile zone centered on downtown.
-       UBS upgraded Rivian to 'Buy' earlier this week, citing solid early R2 demand and a path toward positive automotive gross margins by year-end.
-       BYD, Tesla's chief global rival, reported October new-energy vehicle sales of 490,168 units, up about 11% year over year, with strong overseas shipments near 170,000.
Electric-vehicle developments this week included Tesla's launch of unsupervised Robotaxi service in Fort Worth, a UBS upgrade of Rivian citing early R2 demand, and Citigroup's third-quarter filing that showed increased stakes in some EV names while cutting positions in others.
Tesla Opens Unsupervised Robotaxi Service In Fort Worth
Tesla launched unsupervised Robotaxi rides in Fort Worth this week across an estimated 143-square-mile zone centered on downtown and extending toward Saginaw, White Settlement, Benbrook, Haltom City, and Forest Hill. It is Tesla's seventh U.S. city with unsupervised rides and its fourth in Texas. The launch is the first new market in about three months. Rides are booked through the Robotaxi app with no safety monitor on board, consistent with other Texas operations. Tesla has not confirmed the initial vehicle mix or whether Cybercabs are included at launch.
Rivian Draws Wall Street Optimism
UBS upgraded Rivian to 'Buy' earlier this week, citing solid early R2 demand and a path toward positive automotive gross margins by year-end. The firm has a price target of $17 on the stock and noted that the recent selloff poses a buying opportunity.
In the third quarter, the first full quarter after the company started delivering the R2 SUV to customers, the company's deliveries reached a record 19,248 vehicles, prompting the company to increase its full-year outlook to 67,000–70,000 vehicles.
Tesla's Chinese Rival BYD Clocks Growth; Smaller Startups Report Mixed Performance
BYD, Tesla's chief global rival, reported October new-energy vehicle sales of 490,168 units, up about 11% year over year, with strong overseas shipments near 170,000. Battery electric vehicle deliveries alone amounted to 305,743 units in the month.
Guangzhou-based EV startup XPeng, meanwhile, set a monthly delivery record of 50,237 vehicles in October, up about 20% year over year, with overseas volume also reaching a record.

title: After Earnings, We Raise Our Tesla Stock Fair Value Estimate. Are Shares a Buy?
snippet: Solid results included strong full-self driving software uptake and positive free cash flow.
content:
After Earnings, We Raise Our Tesla Stock Fair Value Estimate. Are Shares a Buy?
Solid results included strong full-self driving software uptake and positive free cash flow.
Tesla released its third-quarter earnings report on Oct. 21. Here’s Morningstar’s take on Tesla’s earnings and stock.
Key Morningstar Metrics for Tesla
- Fair Value Estimate: $475.00
- Morningstar Rating: ★★★
- Morningstar Economic Moat Rating: Narrow
- Morningstar Uncertainty Rating: Very High
What We Thought of Tesla’s Q3 Earnings
Tesla reported solid third-quarter results with positive free cash flow, while long-term growth plans remain intact.
Why it matters: The stock fell 3% after the report as the market reacted to capacity constraints in the company’s auto and battery growth, which could slow near-term growth. We expect Tesla to expand production capacity at all its factories, which should enable delivery growth over the coming years.
- Management also said customers paid for full self-driving software in 75% of North American deliveries during the quarter. This supports our view that Tesla’s FSD autonomous driving software will differentiate it and drive delivery growth.
- Tesla generated positive free cash flow during the quarter, despite higher capital expenditures. Tesla is building new factories, expanding capacity at its current factories, and building compute power to be able to run its autonomous driving and humanoid robot artificial intelligence software.
The bottom line: We raised our fair value estimate for narrow-moat Tesla to $475 per share from $450, on higher full self-driving adoption assumptions and a lower near- and medium-term capital expenditures forecast.
- We point to Robotaxi expansion and progress on Optimus as near-term catalysts for shares. Management said it began production on Optimus and aims to begin selling its humanoid robots by the end of next year. We think this timeline may be optimistic, but we expect Optimus robots to be sold, initially to commercial customers, by the end of the decade, driving long-term profit growth.
The following are excerpts from Morningstar’s company report on Tesla.
Fair Value Estimate for Tesla
With its 3-star rating, we believe Tesla’s stock is fairly valued compared with our long-term fair value estimate of $475 per share. In 2026, we forecast deliveries will grow roughly 10% to nearly 1.8 million versus 1.64 million in 2025. We see lower US deliveries in the first three quarters due to the US EV tax credit expiration in September 2025. However, with full self-driving beginning to be approved in a growing number of countries in Europe, we see strong European deliveries growth more than offsetting a US decline. As Tesla is ramping up production of its new, lower-priced Model Y and Model 3 vehicles, we expect automotive gross margins excluding credits will be in the high teens, slightly below management’s long-term goal of 20%.
Read more about Tesla’s fair value estimate.
Economic Moat Rating
We award Tesla a narrow moat, stemming from intangible assets and a cost advantage. The company’s strong brand cachet as a luxury automaker and its proprietary autonomous driving software command premium pricing, while its electric vehicle manufacturing expertise allows the company to make its vehicles cheaper than competitors.
In all, we think Tesla’s combination of intangible assets and cost advantage will persist and allow the firm to generate excess returns on capital for at least the next 10 years.
Read more about Tesla’s economic moat.
Financial Strength
Tesla is in excellent financial health. Cash, cash equivalents, and investments were $45.5 billion and far exceeded total debt as of Sept. 30. Total debt was a little less than $9.3 billion; however, total recourse debt, which excludes vehicle and energy product financing, was $2 million.
Tesla will largely self-fund its growth. With its positive free cash flow generation and large cash balance, we think Tesla should be able to fund its growth plans over at least the next two years without needing to raise debt.
Historically, Tesla has used credit lines, convertible debt financing, and equity offerings to raise capital. The company currently has $30 billion in untapped credit lines it could use to help fund its robotaxi and humanoid robot growth plans.
Read more about Tesla’s financial strength.
Risk and Uncertainty
We assign Tesla a Very High Uncertainty Rating, as we see a wide range of potential outcomes. The automotive market is highly cyclical and subject to sharp demand declines based on economic conditions. As an EV market leader, Tesla faces growing competition. As new lower-priced EVs enter the market, Tesla has cut prices and offered lower-cost versions of its Model 3 and Model Y vehicles. Further price cuts could reduce profits.
The company is also investing heavily in R&D and capital expenditures to develop autonomous driving software, robotaxis, and humanoid robots, with no guarantee these investments will bear fruit. As of the last Securities and Exchange Commission filing, Tesla’s CEO owns around 20% of the company’s stock and uses it as collateral for personal loans, which raises the risk of a large sale to repay debt.
Tesla also faces political risk related to CEO Elon Musk. Musk served as an advisor to US President Donald Trump but has since made statements against Trump’s policies. Musk also campaigned for the far-right Alternative for Germany party in 2025. These activities risk turning away some consumers from buying a Tesla.
Read more about Tesla’s risk and uncertainty.
TSLA Bulls Say
- Tesla could disrupt multiple industries with its technology for EVs, AVs, batteries, and humanoid robots.
- Tesla’s full self-driving software should generate growing profits in the coming years as the technology continues improving, leading to a robotaxi service and increased adoption by Tesla drivers.
- Tesla’s humanoid robot will create shareholder value as its ability to perform multiple functions will transform manufacturing and be useful to consumers.
TSLA Bears Say
- Traditional automakers and new entrants are investing heavily in EV development, which will result in declining deliveries. This will force Tesla to cut prices due to increased competition, eroding profit margins.
- Tesla’s large investment in autonomous driving software will be value-destructive as the robotaxi product will face delays and competition from Waymo, which already offers a robotaxi service.
- CEO Musk’s political activities will turn consumers away from buying a Tesla in key markets, including the US and Europe, leading to lower sales and profits.

title: RBI Rate Hike Expected in December as Terminal Rate Pegged at 6%
snippet: The Reserve Bank of India is widely expected to implement a 25 basis points rate hike in December, following October's retail ...
content:
The Reserve Bank of India is widely expected to implement a 25 basis points rate hike in December, marking the next step in the monetary policy tightening cycle. According to reports from The Economic Times, Business Standard, and CNBC TV18, this expectation comes after October retail inflation accelerated to 6.09%, breaching the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit for the first time in two years. The Monetary Policy Committee is scheduled to announce its rate decision on December 4, following the committee's last meeting in October where it raised the policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. As per CNBC TV18, CLSA Chief Economist Leif Eskesen noted that recent CPI numbers showed inflation coming in hotter than expected, with both headline and core inflation stronger than anticipated, strengthening the case for another RBI rate hike in December. The RBI is legally required to maintain the headline inflation between 2% and 6%. As per Bloomberg, economists and financial traders expect the RBI to lift the benchmark rate by another 50 to 75 basis points in coming months, potentially taking it as high as 6.25% from the current 5.5%.
Most economists now expect the terminal, or peak, repo rate at 6%, reversing earlier projections of 6.25%. As reported by The Economic Times, Business Standard, and CNBC TV18, while some still see the possibility of the policy rate rising to 6.25%, they consider it a low-probability outcome that would depend entirely on incoming data. State Bank of India chief economic adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh wrote in a report that the balance of probabilities has shifted towards a 25-bps rate hike in December, with further rate hikes in February considered inadvisable given proximity to the union budget. Aditi Nayar, an economist at ratings agency ICRA Ltd. expects inflation to remain above the 6% upper bound of the RBI's tolerance band over the next couple of months, making a December rate hike "almost certain." CNBC TV18 reports that CLSA expects the US Federal Reserve to raise rates by 25 basis points in December, while India's inflation outlook keeps the door open for another RBI rate hike. Bloomberg reports that Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC Holdings Plc, expects an outsized 50-basis-point hike at the RBI's next meeting in December, noting that when both oil and food shocks occur together, the spillover impact can be more meaningful and large.
India's economic growth is expected to face headwinds in the coming fiscal year, with CLSA Chief Economist Leif Eskesen projecting growth to slow to around 6.5% in the next fiscal year. According to CNBC TV18, Eskesen attributed this moderation to the impact of a deficient monsoon on agricultural output, elevated energy prices, tighter monetary policy, and a restrictive fiscal stance. The prospect of higher borrowing costs comes at a challenging time for India's economy, with multiple headwinds creating what economists describe as a "double whammy." According to Business Standard, Apoorva Javadekar, head of research at Shriram Research Pvt Ltd, noted that the combination of rising prices and borrowing costs is "a double whammy for India," particularly impacting consumption, especially in rural areas where agricultural prospects are worsening and inflation is higher than in urban areas. Madhavi Arora, an economist at Emkay Global Financial Services, warned that the intended and unintended consequences of tighter macro-financial conditions will be demand destruction, particularly as supply-side pressures continue to play spoilsport.
Despite economic challenges, India's trade prospects are showing signs of improvement. According to CNBC TV18, CLSA's Leif Eskesen expects the US to push ahead with trade negotiations with India following the midterm elections, creating a more supportive environment for bilateral economic ties. Speaking from the sidelines of CITIC CLSA India Forum, Eskesen said trade discussions are expected to continue alongside efforts to extend the US-China trade truce, reducing uncertainty around global trade. While semiconductor export restrictions to China may remain a difficult area for negotiations, broader trade ties are expected to remain on track. Regarding artificial intelligence, Eskesen noted that recent developments around Nvidia and tighter policy discussions should be viewed as short-term challenges rather than a shift in the long-term outlook for AI. Higher hardware costs, tighter financial conditions and increased regulatory scrutiny are creating "growth strains" for the AI sector, but these developments do not change the long-term investment case, with Eskesen remaining positive on AI in the US, India and other markets over the medium to long term.
The recent correction in crude oil prices has significantly tempered expectations of an aggressive rate hiking cycle, but current levels remain a concern for policymakers. According to The Economic Times and Business Standard, oil prices near $100 a barrel are creating additional strain on the economy, with the Middle East conflict keeping crude elevated and swelling India's import bill. Figures Friday showed India's trade deficit widened to a one-year high in October, adding to the government's subsidy burden. The previous tightening cycle in 2024-25 had benefited from cheaper oil and easing food prices, but this time, the ability to cushion the economy is more constrained. Business Standard reports that food is another source of strain, with severe El Niño conditions threatening global harvests while deficient rains have hurt crops at home. Despite these challenges, India's strong economic fundamentals provide some cushion for the central bank's monetary tightening. As reported by Bloomberg and Business Standard, gross domestic product expanded 7.8% in the April-June quarter and private consumption rose 7.1%, with full-year growth on track to exceed 7%. This strong growth gives the RBI room to sacrifice some demand to bring prices under control.

title: RBI rate hike in December: SBI now expects just 25 bps despite inflation crossing 6% - BusinessToday
snippet: In its latest Ecowrap report dated November 12, SBI Research said the balance of probabilities had shifted decisively towards ...
content:
The revision comes after India's consumer price index (CPI) inflation climbed to a two-year high of 6.09% in October, exceeding the RBI's upper tolerance limit for the first time under the new CPI series.
“When facts change, I change my mind. What do you do sir?” the SBI Research report stated, as it revised its December rate hike forecast from 50 basis points to 25 basis points.
Earlier, the research team had outlined two possibilities: an aggressive 50-bps hike or a 25-bps repo rate increase accompanied by another 25-bps tightening through widening the interest rate corridor.
However, recent domestic and international developments have strengthened the case for a more measured response.
MUST READ: Retail inflation hits two-year high of 6.09% in October, breaches RBI's 6% limit; December rate hike likely
Four factors supporting a smaller rate hike
SBI identified four developments behind its revised forecast.
First, the RBI's efforts to stabilise the rupee and ease liquidity pressures have yielded results. The currency recovered below ₹94 against the dollar before weakening again, while overnight money market rates moderated.
Second, improving foreign capital flows could reduce pressure on the currency. SBI noted foreign institutional investment inflows of approximately $7.68 billion since November 4, alongside a 0.7% appreciation in the rupee.
Third, easing geopolitical tensions have improved the crude oil outlook. Brent crude prices have declined approximately 11% following the US elections, potentially reducing India's imported inflation pressures.
Fourth, SBI expects US Treasury yields to soften, with the benchmark 10-year yield potentially moving towards 4.75%. Indian 10-year government bond yields could settle around 6.75–7%, with a downward bias.
ALSO READ: Inflation bites harder as food prices surge, more rate hikes loom
Inflation remains a major concern
Despite the improving external environment, domestic inflation pressures remain elevated.
Food and beverages inflation reached 8.51% in October, while consumer food price inflation climbed to 8.94%, compared with 7.74% in September.
Onion prices surged 116.22%, followed by garlic at 60.74%, ginger at 48.32% and lemons at 47.3%.
Upasna Bhardwaj, Chief Economist at Kotak Mahindra Bank, expects inflation to remain above 6% over the next few readings, citing adverse base effects, higher food prices and commodity cost pressures.
Madan Sabnavis, Chief Economist at Bank of Baroda, believes the RBI could consider a 25–50 bps hike in December as inflation becomes increasingly broad-based.
Could the repo rate peak at 5.75%?
SBI Research expects inflation to reach approximately 6.3% in November before moderating.
Importantly, it now assigns equal probabilities to the terminal repo rate settling at 6% or a lower 5.75%.
The report also argues against another rate hike in February 2027, favouring a data-dependent approach after December.
For borrowers, the revised forecast suggests a potentially smaller increase in lending rates than previously anticipated, although actual borrowing costs will depend on the RBI's decision and banks' transmission of policy changes.

title: India’s Inflation Challenge: Why the RBI May Need to Raise Rates
snippet: Food inflation hits 8.9%, retail CPI breaches RBI’s 6% limit—economists expect a 25–50 bps repo-rate hike as the MPC meets in ...
content:
India’s Inflation Challenge: Why the RBI May Need to Raise Rates
Food inflation hits 8.9%, retail CPI breaches RBI’s 6% limit—economists expect a 25–50 bps repo-rate hike as the MPC meets in December.
India’s battle against inflation may enter a tougher phase, with economists expecting the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to raise policy rates by 25 to 50 basis points in financial year 2026–27. The concern is driven by persistent food inflation, higher commodity prices and the possibility that price pressures may become more deeply embedded.
Economists expect the RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to consider a further increase at its December meeting. Some experts anticipate a 25-basis-point rise, while others see scope for additional tightening later in the financial year. The expectation follows the MPC’s October meeting, when it maintained a tightening bias and signalled that inflation risks required attention.
Food prices are central to the concern. Food inflation affects household budgets quickly, particularly for lower- and middle-income families, for whom groceries account for a substantial share of monthly spending. When essential items become more expensive, households have less money for other purchases. Businesses also face higher costs, which may be reflected in prices.
The report notes that retail inflation has crossed 7% in six states. It highlights concerns that food inflation could remain elevated as higher commodity prices add to pressure. If households and businesses expect prices to keep rising, wage demands and pricing decisions can reinforce the trend.
India’s situation is connected to the wider global economy. Food and commodity prices are influenced by cross-border factors, including weather disruptions, energy costs, transport expenses, geopolitical tensions and shifts in international supply and demand. Higher global crude oil prices can make production and distribution more expensive. Imported edible oils, fertilisers and industrial materials can transmit external price pressures into domestic markets. Currency movements matter: when the rupee weakens against major currencies, imports become costlier.
These global pressures intersect with domestic conditions such as monsoon performance, crop arrivals, food supply management and consumer demand. A favourable harvest can moderate prices, but disruptions in production or distribution may reverse that relief. The inflation outlook is shaped by several moving parts, not one indicator.
Central banks worldwide face a similar balancing act. They must prevent inflation from becoming entrenched without unnecessarily weakening economic activity. Higher interest rates can cool demand by making loans more expensive and encouraging saving. However, monetary policy cannot directly increase vegetable supplies, repair supply chains or reduce international energy prices. Its impact is indirect and takes time.
Economists expect the RBI to remain cautious. State Bank of India’s assessment points to a possible 25-basis-point increase in December, while other economists see further action as dependent on incoming data. Some forecasts suggest cumulative increases of around 50 basis points in the coming months, although the final decision rests with the MPC.
The RBI must weigh price stability against the need to sustain growth. A rate increase could help anchor inflation expectations, but it may also raise borrowing costs for households and companies. The coming months will test the central bank’s judgement. Food supplies, commodity trends, currency movements and global developments will shape its choices. For consumers and businesses, inflation remains a key economic risk, and India’s response will depend as much on conditions at home as on forces beyond its borders in the months ahead.
(The writer is Consulting Editor - ShikshaLoan.com, a seasoned Banker and Education Loan Specialist. He writes about education loan requirements for studying abroad, financial policy, digital services, and public infrastructure in India.)

title: SBI Halves RBI Rate Hike Forecast to 0.25% Amid Easing Pressures
snippet: SBI economists revise RBI's December rate hike forecast to 0.25% from 0.50%, citing improved external conditions, rupee stability, and foreign inflows.
content:
SBI Halves RBI Rate Hike Forecast to 0.25% Amid Easing Pressures
x
SBI economists revise RBI's December rate hike forecast to 0.25% from 0.50%, citing improved external conditions, rupee stability, and foreign inflows.
				
		
Key Points
- SBI economists have revised their forecast for RBI's December rate hike from 0.50% to 0.25%.
- The revision is attributed to improved external conditions, increased foreign fund inflows, and easing pressure on the rupee.
- Despite recent high inflation prints, SBI suggests a 50:50 chance the December hike could be the last in the current cycle.
- Global factors like declining crude oil prices and softening US Treasury yields also contribute to the revised outlook.
- Foreign institutional investors have infused significant capital into Indian markets, further supporting the rupee.
In a note, they attributed the revision to improved external conditions, revival in foreign fund inflows and easing pressure on the rupee.
Interestingly, the note got published hours after headline inflation shooting the 6 per cent tolerance band set for the RBI, and analysts' expectations of more such prints being in offing.
The SBI report said that there is a "50:50 probability" of the December hike being the final one in the current cycle, as it said that the terminal repo rate can be at 5.75 per cent as well.
The RBI hiked the benchmark policy rate by 0.25 percentage point to 5.50 per cent in October, its first hike in nearly four years, while signalling that further rate hikes could follow amid rising inflation, a weak rupee and high crude oil prices.
SBI Research expects inflation to remain above 6 per cent in November before moderating thereafter. It said trends in the first two weeks of November's price data from the Department of Consumer Affairs also indicate that inflation could remain elevated.
The department had earlier outlined two possible policy options for the December monetary policy committee (MPC) meeting -- an aggressive 0.50 per cent or a 0.25 per cent increase accompanied by another 0.25 per cent adjustment through corridor widening.
However, recent developments have shifted the balance of probabilities towards a 0.25 per cent, it said.
SBI Research said the RBI's efforts to manage rupee volatility have yielded results, with the domestic currency moving below 94 against the US dollar, while liquidity pressures have also eased.
The call money rate, which had risen to as high as 5.8 per cent in the last week of October, subsequently declined to below the marginal standing facility (MSF) rate of 5.44 per cent, it said.
The improvement in the external environment and revival in capital flows are expected to further ease pressure on the rupee. Foreign institutional investors have infused around USD 7.65 billion into Indian markets since November 6, according to the report.
The correction in artificial intelligence-related valuations globally could also improve India's relative market valuations and support foreign fund inflows, it said.
On the commodity front, the prospect of de-escalation in the US-Iran conflict has improved the outlook for crude oil prices. Crude prices have declined 11 per cent since the US elections, to around USD 87 per barrel, the report said.
SBI Research also expects US Treasury yields to soften following the Democrats' victory in the US mid-term elections, with the 10-year yield likely to move towards 4.75 per cent.
For India, it expects the 10-year government bond yield to settle in the 6.75-7 per cent range, but with a clear downward bias. Importantly, expectations of three to four successive rate hikes, which had gained traction earlier, now appear to be an "outlier", the report said.
