title: Outlook
snippet: Apr 29, 2026 · Central bank buying is expected to be solid at levels close to those in 2025. Demand shows good traction despite price volatility and continued geoeconomic risks could provide additional upside. However, periodic mobilisation of gold reserves on further supply shocks cannot be discounted.
content:
Data revisions for Q1, including a reclassification from central banks to OTC, are available on Gold Demand Trends Q2 2026
Outlook
29 April, 2026
Geopolitical factors are expected to remain front and centre in driving gold demand for 2026 and beyond. This supports continued central bank net buying, broad global gold ETF inflows, and bar and coin accumulation. Recycling is expected to see a restrained increase in 2026. High prices are likely to continue taking their toll on jewellery. Mine supply is expected to edge higher again in response to high prices and margins.
- Government bond yields are likely to stay elevated until a clearer path for policy rates emerges as central banks grapple with supply shocks from the US-Israel-Iran war and a positive stock-bond correlation undermines the appeal of bonds as a hedge
- The geopolitical risk premium that has helped lift gold over the past few years is set to continue and possibly expand as the year progresses
- As a result, demand for gold ETFs and OTC could be positive but lower than in 2025. Bar and coin demand, on the other hand, is likely to feature more in 2026 as high prices, a lack of viable alternative investments in some markets, inflation fears and heightened uncertainty continue to attract both savers and speculators
- Overall, Asian demand will likely remain a key source of strength in investment, as concern over global geopolitics fuels demand for effective risk hedges
- Jewellery spend is likely to be resilient, absent economic shocks, but tonnage demand is expected to slip further as high prices, and regional tax policies, continue to bite
- Central bank buying is expected to be solid at levels close to those in 2025. Demand shows good traction despite price volatility and continued geoeconomic risks could provide additional upside. However, periodic mobilisation of gold reserves on further supply shocks cannot be discounted
- Mine production is likely to rise modestly again in 2026, although we are monitoring the effects of energy shortages on operations in some regions. Recycling is rising but is expected to be constrained by low near-market stocks, expectations of continued price strength, and a likely imbedded geopolitical risk premium.
Investment
The geopolitical risk premium that has helped lift gold over the past few years is set to continue and perhaps expand as the year progresses with uncertainty about the new Federal Reserve chair, including the timing of his confirmation, as well as strained US-China relations all potentially contributing. And while questions have been raised about gold’s lack of positive response to the war in the Middle East thus far, this initial move is not unprecedented. However, we would expect a prolonged conflict or a wider spill-over effect on the global economy to provoke a more visible positive reaction from gold.
This is likely to support global gold ETF, bar and coins as it has done to date. However, ETF demand may not reach the heights of 2025 as rates may stay higher for longer. This is likely to weigh on gold demand from some investors, unless the Middle East crisis exerts a supply shock large enough to tilt economies towards recession.
The combination of these factors is likely to see investment demand remain positive but below 2025 levels.
Indian bar and coin demand and local gold ETFs started the year on a strong footing. The shift into investment is likely to continue in 2026 on the back of price momentum, geopolitical risk and relatively less attractive investment alternatives.
Broad Asian investment demand across the board, particularly in China, should similarly benefit from price momentum, rising safe-haven demand and a lack of alternative investment prospects.
Fabrication
Jewellery demand was softer than anticipated in Q1, leading us to downgrade our full-year expected fabrication figure.
Persistent high prices (with y-t-d gains already matching last year) remain a headwind to global demand. And the potential for significant global economic fallout from the Middle East conflict may add to the pressure on consumer sentiment as well as the capacity for discretionary spending.
China’s recent VAT policy change remains an obstacle for jewellery demand in that market, likely funnelling further potential purchases towards lower-premium bars and coins; a trend that is also increasingly evident in India.
Central banks
Initial estimates of central bank net buying in Q1 are reassuringly robust, particularly in light of recent price volatility and notable mobilisation of reserves. But we don’t rule out further tactical rebalancing activity as a result of Middle East disruptions, liquidity needs and foreign exchange management. More generally, we view geoeconomic uncertainty as providing longer-term support to gold demand in the sector. Our full-year target remains similar to last year, between 700-900t.
Supply
Mine production is likely to see modest growth again in 2026 as high prices drive incremental increases in both the LSM and ASGM segments. Some production disruptions from diesel shortages may materialise in mines in Oceania and Asia which could temper this growth. And in the longer term challenges around finding, permitting, financing and building new LSM projects continue.
Recycling
Recycling has started to pick up, perhaps partly on concerns about gold’s volatility and the squeeze on consumer wallets from higher energy prices. A prolonged stand-off between the US and Iran could elicit more selling back. And supply from India could jump if collateralised loans come under pressure. But if gold prices stabilise – and particularly if the path to higher prices looks to be more certain – the Q1 bump in recycling will more likely be a one off.

title: AMD beats expectations as agentic AI sparks its data center revenue growth engines - SiliconANGLE
snippet: rose more than 5% in late trading today after it delivered solid third-quarter earnings and revenue today, with data center ...
content:
AMD beats expectations as agentic AI sparks its data center revenue growth engines
Shares of the chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices Inc. rose more than 5% in late trading today after it delivered solid third-quarter earnings and revenue today, with data center sales almost doubling from a year ago.
The company reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $2.09 per share, easily beating Wall Street’s forecast of $1.95 per share. Revenue for the period jumped 45% from a year earlier, to $13.38 billion, ahead of the $13.09 billion analyst consensus estimate. All told, the company’s net income for the quarter came to $3.47 billion, up 77% from the previous year when it posted a profit of just $1.96 billion.
The star performer in the quarter was AMD’s data center business unit, which accounted for 64% of its overall revenue, up from just 47% one year ago. After spending years trying to compete with Nvidia Corp.’s graphics processing units for artificial intelligence market share, the company’s traditional central processing units or CPUs are suddenly back in vogue thanks to the emergence of agentic AI applications such as Meta Platforms Inc.’s Muse. Autonomous AI agents can run much more efficiently on CPUs than they can on GPUs, boosting demand for the chips.
Looking ahead, AMD expects its server revenue to double year-over-year in fiscal 2027, with AI growth likely to accelerate even faster than the company projected just three months ago. “Adoption is just starting and we expect demand to grow sharply as agents are deployed more broadly and take on more complex work,” AMD Chief Executive Lisa Su (pictured) said on a conference call with analysts.
AMD’s data center story isn’t all about CPUs, though. The company also sells GPUs, including bundles of them shipped inside data center-ready rack-scale systems called Helios, and that system’s popularity is growing fast.
Su said Anthropic PBC, OpenAI Group PBC, Microsoft Corp., Oracle Corp. and Meta are all using AMD Helios systems in their data centers. Last week, Meta said its first Helion racks are already up and running as it revealed that AMD invested $1 billion in its latest equity offering.
The chipmaker has also committed to a $5 billion investment in Anthropic, which last week revealed the long-awaited prospectus for its upcoming initial public offering.
AMD delivered its latest earnings report just days after its rival Intel Corp. did the same. Intel also posted strong data center revenue growth, but its stock fell more than 30% on Friday on weak guidance and concerns about its ability to meet demand for its products.
But Su said AMD had no such problems. Last month she made a high-profile visit to Taiwan, where she held meetings with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and a number of supply chain partners, and said after the trip that the company plans to substantially increase its supply in the coming year. “We have worked across our supply chain to secure the wafers, substrates, advanced packaging, memory and other key components needed to support much higher growth next year,” Su added.
AMD’s results will go some way toward reassuring investors who have become increasingly nervous about the direction of the AI industry and whether the hundreds of billions of dollars being spent on it each year is actually going to generate a return on their investments, said eMarketer analyst Jacob Bourne. “The results are a test of AMD’s own performance and the broader AI trade, and its data center and revenue beats will encourage investors after the recent semiconductor selloff,” he added.
Though AMD is far from immune to the recent volatility that has afflicted AI-related stocks, its future still looks increasingly rosy for now. “Demand for AI computing is not going to fall off a cliff, and AMD has the competitive products and major customer relationships to capitalize on that demand,” Bourne said.
Strength in the data center unit is helping AMD to ride out difficulties in its traditional market for personal computers, which is the reason for Intel’s poor outlook. During the second quarter, global PC shipments fell 4% from a year earlier, with buyers dissuaded by the rising cost of components such as memory chips, according to data from Counterpoint Research.
Along with Intel, AMD is a leading manufacturer of the x86 CPUs that power most of the world’s computers and laptops. The company reports PC chip revenue within a segment that also includes its chips for games consoles, and that unit saw its revenue decline 8% from a year earlier, to $3.7 billion. Gaming revenue fell 40% from the previous year.
For the current quarter, AMD is targeting revenue of abouot $17 billion at the midpoint of its guidance range, ahead of the Street’s $16.2 billion consensus estimate. The company also sees its gross margins coming in at 55%, just below the Street’s forecast of 55.3%.
AMD was busy on the acquisition front during the quarter. In September it revealed it’s going to buy World Labs Inc. for $8.2 billion in an all-stock deal. The San Francisco-based AI lab, founded by the AI industry luminary Fei-Fei Li, has developed world models that can simulate 3D environments to support the training of intelligent robots and other physical AI applications.
The company also acquired a startup called Taalas Inc. that makes specialized model-specific integrated circuits, which are essentially chips that can be customized to run a specific AI model more efficiently. That acquisition should help to boost AMD’s position in AI inference. AMD also invested in the AI image generation model maker Stability AI Ltd., which raised $76 million in funding in August.

title: AMD's Lisa Su says largest customers are already talking MI500 and MI600
snippet: AMD CEO Lisa Su reveals talks with top customers on MI500 and MI600 chips, signaling how AI hardware is now won years before ...
content:
AMD’s Lisa Su says largest customers are already talking MI500 and MI600
AMD is in active discussions with top clients about Instinct GPUs that are still years from shipping, as hyperscalers plan AI infrastructure far ahead
AMD CEO Lisa Su says the company’s biggest customers are already asking about chips that won’t exist for years. According to Su, AMD is in active talks with its largest clients about the MI500, the MI600 and products beyond them.
“We’re in very active dialogs with our largest customers on MI500 and MI600 and beyond.” – Lisa Su, CEO, AMD
What AMD is actually selling
The near-term piece is the MI400 series, built on the CDNA 5 architecture. AMD’s roadmap has it shipping in volume by 2026.
Next up is the MI500 series, scheduled for a 2027 launch. It is built on CDNA 6 architecture, uses an advanced 2nm manufacturing process, and pairs with HBM4E memory.
The MI500’s stated ambition is large. AMD is targeting more than 2,000× higher inference throughput than the MI300X within four years.
After the MI500 comes the MI600 series, which is expected in 2028. Su’s comments suggest customers are already factoring that generation into their planning too.
Helios and the rack-scale pitch
The company plans annual releases of new Helios rack-scale AI platforms through at least 2030. Each Helios system integrates Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs and Pensando networking into one package.
Meta is the showcase customer here. The company has already begun deploying Helios systems and has contributed to the development of AMD’s latest GPUs.
AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing.
Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.
Meta has also deployed millions of EPYC processors from AMD. It is described as an integral partner in custom Instinct GPU deployment, which makes it less of a customer and more of a co-designer.
The numbers behind the confidence
Su’s comments come with financial backing. AMD reported Q1 AI-related revenue of $5.8 billion in 2026, a 57% year-over-year increase.
MI300-series accelerators made up approximately 73% of that AI revenue.
What this means
Talks are not orders, though. Su described dialogs, not signed commitments, and the gap between a roadmap slide and a shipped product is where chip companies historically stumble.
The MI500 depends on a 2nm process and HBM4E memory, both advanced technologies, and any delay ripples through every customer’s build-out plan.
The Meta relationship is the template to watch. If AMD can replicate that co-development model with other large customers, the MI500 and MI600 conversations could turn into the kind of multi-generation commitments that reshape market share.
The near-term checkpoint is the MI400 volume ramp in 2026. If that goes smoothly, Su’s talk of MI500, MI600 and beyond starts to look less like ambition and more like a schedule.

title: AMD Delivers Leadership Portfolio of Data Center AI Solutions with AMD Instinct MI300 Series
snippet: Dec 6, 2023 · “AMD Instinct MI300 Series accelerators are designed with our most advanced technologies, delivering leadership performance, and will be in large scale cloud and enterprise deployments,” said Victor Peng, president, AMD.
content:
— Dell Technologies, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Lenovo, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, Supermicro and others showcase AMD hardware for high performance computing and generative AI —
— ROCm 6 open software ecosystem combines next-gen hardware and software to deliver ~8x generational performance increase, power advancements in generative AI and simplify deployment of AMD AI solutions —
SANTA CLARA, Calif., Dec. 06, 2023 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Today, AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) announced the availability of the AMD Instinct™ MI300X accelerators – with industry leading memory bandwidth for generative AI1 and leadership performance for large language model (LLM) training and inferencing – as well as the AMD Instinct™ MI300A accelerated processing unit (APU) – combining the latest AMD CDNA™ 3 architecture and “Zen 4” CPUs to deliver breakthrough performance for HPC and AI workloads.
“AMD Instinct MI300 Series accelerators are designed with our most advanced technologies, delivering leadership performance, and will be in large scale cloud and enterprise deployments,” said Victor Peng, president, AMD. “By leveraging our leadership hardware, software and open ecosystem approach, cloud providers, OEMs and ODMs are bringing to market technologies that empower enterprises to adopt and deploy AI-powered solutions.”
Customers leveraging the latest AMD Instinct accelerator portfolio include Microsoft, which recently announced the new Azure ND MI300x v5 Virtual Machine (VM) series, optimized for AI workloads and powered by AMD Instinct MI300X accelerators. Additionally, El Capitan – a supercomputer powered by AMD Instinct MI300A APUs and housed at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory – is expected to be the second exascale-class supercomputer powered by AMD and expected to deliver more than two exaflops of double precision performance when fully deployed. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure plans to add AMD Instinct MI300X-based bare metal instances to the company’s high-performance accelerated computing instances for AI. MI300X-based instances are planned to support OCI Supercluster with ultrafast RDMA networking.
Several major OEMs also showcased accelerated computing systems, in tandem with the AMD Advancing AI event. Dell showcased the Dell PowerEdge XE9680 server featuring eight AMD Instinct MI300 Series accelerators and the new Dell Validated Design for Generative AI with AMD ROCm-powered AI frameworks. HPE recently announced the HPE Cray Supercomputing EX255a, the first supercomputing accelerator blade powered by AMD Instinct MI300A APUs, which will become available in early 2024. Lenovo announced its design support for the new AMD Instinct MI300 Series accelerators with planned availability in the first half of 2024. Supermicro announced new additions to its H13 generation of accelerated servers powered by 4th Gen AMD EPYC™ CPUs and AMD Instinct MI300 Series accelerators.
AMD Instinct MI300X
AMD Instinct MI300X accelerators are powered by the new AMD CDNA 3 architecture. When compared to previous generation AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators, MI300X delivers nearly 40% more compute units2, 1.5x more memory capacity, 1.7x more peak theoretical memory bandwidth3 as well as support for new math formats such as FP8 and sparsity; all geared towards AI and HPC workloads.
Today’s LLMs continue to increase in size and complexity, requiring massive amounts of memory and compute. AMD Instinct MI300X accelerators feature a best-in-class 192 GB of HBM3 memory capacity as well as 5.3 TB/s peak memory bandwidth2 to deliver the performance needed for increasingly demanding AI workloads. The AMD Instinct Platform is a leadership generative AI platform built on an industry standard OCP design with eight MI300X accelerators to offer an industry leading 1.5TB of HBM3 memory capacity. The AMD Instinct Platform’s industry standard design allows OEM partners to design-in MI300X accelerators into existing AI offerings and simplify deployment and accelerate adoption of AMD Instinct accelerator-based servers.
Compared to the Nvidia H100 HGX, the AMD Instinct Platform can offer a throughput increase of up to 1.6x when running inference on LLMs like BLOOM 176B4 and is the only option on the market capable of running inference for a 70B parameter model, like Llama2, on a single MI300X accelerator; simplifying enterprise-class LLM deployments and enabling outstanding TCO.
AMD Instinct MI300A
The AMD Instinct MI300A APUs, the world’s first data center APU for HPC and AI, leverage 3D packaging and the 4th Gen AMD Infinity Architecture to deliver leadership performance on critical workloads sitting at the convergence of HPC and AI. MI300A APUs combine high-performance AMD CDNA 3 GPU cores, the latest AMD “Zen 4” x86-based CPU cores and 128GB of next-generation HBM3 memory, to deliver ~1.9x the performance-per-watt on FP32 HPC and AI workloads, compared to previous gen AMD Instinct MI250X5.
Energy efficiency is of utmost importance for the HPC and AI communities, however these workloads are extremely data- and resource-intensive. AMD Instinct MI300A APUs benefit from integrating CPU and GPU cores on a single package delivering a highly efficient platform while also providing the compute performance to accelerate training the latest AI models. AMD is setting the pace of innovation in energy efficiency with the company’s 30x25 goal, aiming to deliver a 30x energy efficiency improvement in server processors and accelerators for AI-training and HPC from 2020-20256.
The APU advantage means that AMD Instinct MI300A APUs feature unified memory and cache resources giving customers an easily programmable GPU platform, highly performant compute, fast AI training and impressive energy efficiency to power the most demanding HPC and AI workloads.
ROCm Software and Ecosystem Partners
AMD announced the latest AMD ROCm™ 6 open software platform as well as the company’s commitment to contribute state-of-the-art libraries to the open-source community, furthering the company’s vision of open-source AI software development. ROCm 6 software represents a significant leap forward for AMD software tools, increasing AI acceleration performance by ~8x when running on MI300 Series accelerators in Llama 2 text generation compared to previous generation hardware and software7. Additionally, ROCm 6 adds support for several new key features for generative AI including FlashAttention, HIPGraph and vLLM, among others. As such, AMD is uniquely positioned to leverage the most broadly used open-source AI software models, algorithms and frameworks – such as Hugging Face, PyTorch, TensorFlow and others – driving innovation, simplifying the deployment of AMD AI solutions and unlocking the true potential of generative AI.
AMD also continues to invest in software capabilities through the acquisitions of Nod.AI and Mipsology as well as through strategic ecosystem partnerships such as Lamini – running LLMs for enterprise customers – and MosaicML – leveraging AMD ROCm to enable LLM training on AMD Instinct accelerators with zero code changes.

Supercharging AI and HPC
AMD Instinct™ MI300 Series accelerators are uniquely well-suited to power even the most demanding AI and HPC workloads, offering exceptional compute performance, large memory density with high bandwidth, and support for specialized data formats.
Under the Hood
AMD Instinct MI300 Series accelerators are built on AMD CDNA™ 3 architecture, which offers Matrix Core Technologies and support for a broad range of precision capabilities—from the highly efficient INT8 and FP8 (including sparsity support for AI), to the most demanding FP64 for HPC.
Meet the Series
Explore AMD Instinct MI300 Series accelerators, AMD Instinct MI300 Series Platforms, and AMD Instinct MI300A APU.
Meet the AMD Instinct™ MI325X Accelerators
The AMD Instinct™ MI325X GPU accelerator sets new standards in AI performance with 3rd Gen AMD CDNA™ architecture, delivering incredible performance and efficiency for training and inference. With industry leading 256 GB HBM3E memory and 6 TB/s bandwidth, they optimize performance and help reduce TCO.1

title: AMD Takes On Nvidia with New GPU for AI
snippet: Dec 6, 2023 · AMD introduces two new data center processors for AI and HPC workloads with support from Microsoft Azure, Meta, Oracle Cloud, Dell, HPE and others. Aug 17, 2024 · DATA CENTER APU & DISCRETE GPU Focused improvements on unified memory, AI data format performance, and in-node networking The AMD Instinct MI300 Series GPUs are based on the AMD CDNA 3 architecture which was designed to deliver leadership performance for HPC, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning (ML) workloads.
content:
AMD Takes On Nvidia with New GPU for AI
AMD introduces two new data center processors for AI and HPC workloads with support from Microsoft Azure, Meta, Oracle Cloud, Dell, HPE and others.
AMD today announced the availability of AMD Instinct MI300X, a new powerful data center GPU that the company hopes will grab market share from Nvidia in the lucrative AI chip market.
The MI300X GPU, designed for cloud providers and enterprises, is built for generative AI applications and outperforms Nvidia’s H100 GPU in two key metrics: memory capacity and memory bandwidth, which enables AMD to deliver comparable AI training performance and significantly higher AI inferencing performance, AMD executives said.
“It’s the highest performance accelerator in the world for generative AI,” said AMD CEO Lisa Su at the company’s “Advancing AI” event in San Jose, Calif. today.
AMD today also announced the availability of AMD Instinct MI300A, an integrated CPU and GPU chip that the company calls an accelerated processing unit (APU). It is designed for high-performance computing (HPC) and AI workloads, and is optimized for performance and energy-efficiency, the company said.
Analysts say AMD has introduced competitive AI chips and has good potential for making inroads into the market, particularly with Nvidia struggling to meet the enormous demand for its popular H100 GPU because of supply chain constraints. Nvidia currently dominates with more than 70% of the AI chip market, according to analyst firm Omdia.
“AMD is taking advantage of Nvidia’s inability to fully meet the needs of the market,” says Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy. “Nvidia can’t make them fast enough. They literally have backlogs that go quarters long of customers that want the H100. AMD comes along and says, ‘guess what? We have a competitive product.’ And AMD is doing it through better performance and what I believe will be better price/performance.”
AMD did not announce pricing for the MI300X. But the H100 often costs more than $30,000.
Kimball expects AMD will see success with the new MI300 Series processors – and so does AMD, which expects strong sales. During AMD’s third quarter earnings call on Oct. 31, Su said data center GPU revenue will exceed $2 billion in 2024 and that the MI300 line will be the fastest product to ramp to $1 billion in sales in AMD history.
Kimball said he doesn’t doubt that AMD will reach that sales goal “because there is such a hunger for GPUs for AI.”
“There are two factors going on: people don’t want to wait for Nvidia, and the industry doesn’t want to be locked into Nvidia,” he said. “So both these factors are going to accelerate the adoption of the MI300 among hyperscalers and within the enterprise.”
AI: Transformational, But Will Require Infrastructure Investments
During her speech today, Su said AI is the single most transformational technology over the past 50 years. “Maybe the only thing that has been close has been the introduction of the internet, but what’s different about AI is that the adoption rate is much, much faster,” she said.
Last year, AMD estimated that the data center AI accelerated market would grow 50% over the next few years, from $30 billion in 2023 to $150 billion in 2027. Today, she updated that prediction, saying the data center accelerator market will grow more than 70% annually over the next four years and reach more than $400 billion in 2027.
"The key to all of this is generative AI," Su said. "It requires a significant investment in new infrastructure. And that's to enable training and all of the inference that's needed. And that market is just huge.”
More Details on the MI300X and MI300A
The MI300 Series of processors, which AMD calls “accelerators,” was first announced nearly six months ago when Su detailed the chipmaker’s strategy for AI computing in the data center.
AMD has built momentum since then. Today’s announcement that MI300X and MI300A are shipping and in production comes with widespread industry support from large cloud companies such as Meta, Microsoft Azure and Oracle Cloud and hardware makers such as Dell, Hewlett-Packard Enterprise, Lenovo and Supermicro.
The AMD Instinct MI300X GPU, powered by the new AMD CDNA 3 architecture, offers 192 GB of HBM3 memory capacity, which is 2.4 times more than Nvidia’s H100’s 80 GB of HBM3 memory capacity. The M1300X reaches 5.3 TB/s peak memory bandwidth, which is 1.6 times more than Nvidia’s H100’s 3.3 TB/s.
In a media briefing before today’s AMD event, Brad McCredie, AMD’s corporate vice president of data center GPU, said the MI300X GPU will still have more memory bandwidth and memory capacity than Nvidia’s next-generation H200 GPU, which is expected next year.
When Nvidia announced plans for the H200 in November, it said the H200 will feature 141 GB of HBM3 memory and 4.8 TB/s of memory bandwidth.
Moving forward, McCredie expects fierce competition between the two companies on the GPU front.
“We do not expect (Nvidia) to stand still. We know how to go fast, too,” he said. “Nvidia has accelerated their roadmap once, recently. We fully expect them to keep pushing hard. We’re going to keep pushing hard, so we fully expect to stay ahead. They may leapfrog. We’ll leapfrog back.”
The AMD Instinct MI300A APU, built with AMD CDNA 3 GPU cores and the latest AMD Zen 4 x86-based CPU cores, offers 128GB of HBM3 memory. When compared to the previous generation M250X processor, the MI300A offers 1.9 times more performance per watt on HPC and AI workloads, the company said.
“At the node level, the MI300A has twice the HPC performance-per-watt of the nearest competitor,” said Forrest Norrod, executive vice president and general manager of AMD’s data center solutions business group, during today’s AMD event. “Customers can thus fit more nodes in their overall facility power budget and better support their sustainability goals.”
The Energy Department’s Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory is using MI300A APUs to build its El Capitan supercomputer, which will surpass speeds of more than 2 exaflops per second and will become the nation’s third exascale supercomputer when it debuts in 2024.
AMD Beefs Up Software Ecosystem
To increase adoption of the new MI300 Series chips, AMD today announced enhancements to its software ecosystem. The company announced ROCm 6, the latest version of its open-source software stack. ROCm 6 – which is a layer of software for GPUs to support computational workloads – has been optimized for generative AI, particularly large language models (LLMs), the company said.
ROCm 6 software, paired with MI300 Series accelerators, will deliver an eight times performance improvement when compared with ROCm 5 and the previous generation MI250 accelerator, the company said.
Cloud and Hardware Maker Support
During the AMD event, executives from hyperscalers and hardware vendors announced plans to include the MI300 Series accelerators in their offerings.
For example, Microsoft today said its new Azure virtual machine offering powered by MI300X is available in preview today. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure plans to offer MI300X-based bare metal instances for AI. And Meta said it is adding MI300X to its data centers to power AI inferencing workloads.
On the hardware front, Dell unveiled the Dell PowerEdge XE9680 server, featuring eight MI300 Series accelerators. HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro also announced it will support MI300 Series accelerators in its product portfolios.

title: TaMo PV narrows Q2 loss to ₹5,451 cr as JLR recovery offsets costs
snippet: Exceptional charges of ₹6,738 crore weigh on earnings as JLR cuts FY27 margin guidance to 2-3 per cent amid commodity cost ...
content:
TaMo PV narrows Q2 loss to ₹5,451 cr as JLR recovery offsets costs
Exceptional charges of ₹6,738 crore weigh on earnings as JLR cuts FY27 margin guidance to 2-3 per cent amid commodity cost pressures and challenging global market conditions
Listen to This Article
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV) reported a consolidated net loss of ₹5,451 crore from continuing operations for the second quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27), narrowing from a loss of ₹6,368 crore a year earlier, as recovering Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) volumes helped offset restructuring costs and asset impairments.
 
Consolidated revenue from operations rose 34 percent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) to ₹96,920 crore from ₹72,349 crore, supported by a recovery at JLR following the cyberattack-related disruption in the year-ago quarter and strong growth in the domestic passenger vehicle (PV) business.
 
The company incurred exceptional charges of ₹6,738 crore during the quarter, primarily comprising employee separation costs and asset impairments. On a reported basis, the company posted a consolidated net loss attributable to shareholders of ₹5,531 crore, compared with a profit of ₹76,170 crore a year earlier. However, the year-ago figure included a substantial exceptional gain arising from the demerger of its commercial vehicle (CV) business, making the reported profit figures not directly comparable.
 
The consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (Ebitda) margin stood at 6.2 per cent, an improvement of 630 basis points (bps) Y-o-Y, largely reflecting recovery from the cyber-incident at JLR in the corresponding period last year. Sequentially, margins were affected by an adverse product mix and persistent commodity cost pressures.
 
TMPV shares fell 3.31 per cent to close at ₹287.40 on Friday.
Also Read
JLR reported revenue of £5.89 billion during the quarter, up 20.3 per cent Y-o-Y, as wholesale volumes recovered in the UK and overseas markets. However, lower volumes in China and West Asia, along with an adverse market and model mix, continued to affect profitability. JLR's profit before tax (PBT) and exceptional items stood at £6 million, against a loss of £485 million a year earlier. Its Ebitda margin improved to 6.6 percent.
The British luxury-car maker recognised exceptional charges of £530 million during the quarter towards restructuring activities, including employee separation costs and asset impairments.
 
JLR management said £295 million of the exceptional charges related to its voluntary redundancy programme targeting around 4,000 employees. Around 3,000 employees had already signed up, with the majority expected to leave on November 30. The remaining charges largely comprised asset writedowns.
 
The management said China remained a challenging market, and the company could not be certain that the decline in sales had bottomed out. JLR was reassessing its approach to the Chinese market while maintaining disciplined dealer inventories and avoiding excessive discounting.
Amid continuing geopolitical uncertainties, inflationary pressures, and market challenges, JLR revised its full-year guidance to an adjusted Ebit margin of 2-3 per cent and free cash outflow of around £1.25 billion.
 
P B Balaji, chief executive officer (CEO) of JLR, said the company delivered positive operating profits in Q2 and the first half (H1) of FY27 despite global challenges.
 
"With the proposed arrival of Range Rover GT and a new electric Defender product in the new year, we are entering a phase of exciting product launches," Balaji said.
 
He added that the company's growth plans for the US and its Enterprise Missions cost-reduction programme, aimed at reducing breakeven volumes to 300,000 units, positioned it for consistent, cash-generating growth.
The domestic PV business, meanwhile, recorded its highest ever quarterly revenue of ₹20,423 crore, growing 50.9 per cent Y-o-Y. However, its Ebitda margin contracted by 180 bps to 4 per cent, while its Ebit margin remained negative at 0.3 per cent.
 
Shailesh Chandra, managing director (MD) and CEO of TMPV, said the company had been able to offset only around 40 per cent of the impact of rising commodity costs through calibrated price increases and cost reductions, absorbing the remaining pressure on its profitability. Steel, rubber, and copper prices were expected to remain elevated in Q3FY27, although some moderation was visible in precious metals.
The company is also considering a larger price increase in Q4FY27. "In Q4, we might go for slightly higher price increase as compared to what we have been taking," Chandra said during the earnings call. He expects profitability to remain around current levels in Q3 before improving in Q4 through pricing and cost-reduction measures.
 
Chandra said the company recorded quarterly sales of over 200,000 units, with volumes growing 40 per cent Y-o-Y. Electric vehicle (EV) sales rose 90 per cent during the quarter.
 
He clarified that the company was not sacrificing profitability to gain market share. With demand currently exceeding supply, market-share gains were a consequence of meeting customer demand rather than aggressive discounting. Chandra also expects India's PV industry to grow around 12-13 per cent in FY27, with growth moderating to approximately 5 per cent in H2FY27 because of a higher base. He said discounts had been declining over the past two to three quarters and did not foresee a return to widespread discounting in the near term.

title: JLR's 20% revenue growth supports Tata Motors PV's Q2 performance as revenue rises 34% to ₹96,920 crore
snippet: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reported Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹96,920 crore, though exceptional costs led to a consolidated net ...
content:
ADVERTISEMENT
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (TMPVL), formerly Tata Motors Limited, reported a 34% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to ₹96,920 crore for Q2 FY27, while consolidated EBITDA margin improved 630 basis points to 6.2%. However, exceptional expenses of approximately ₹6,700 crore, primarily towards employee separation costs and asset impairments, pushed the company's consolidated loss before tax to ₹6,335 crore.
Consolidated profit before tax and exceptional items stood at ₹403 crore during the quarter, compared with a loss of ₹5,482 crore in the corresponding period last year. The improvement in operating performance was largely supported by a recovery in Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), which had faced a cyber incident during the same period last year.
Consolidated EBIT margin also improved 790 basis points year-on-year to 1.1%. However, sequentially, margins remained under pressure due to an adverse product mix and continued commodity cost inflation.
The company reported a consolidated net loss of ₹5,500 crore for the quarter, after recognising a deferred tax asset. Its consolidated free cash flow stood at a negative ₹6,300 crore, taking net debt to ₹50,800 crore as of September 30, 2026.
Dhiman Gupta, Chief Financial Officer, TMPVL, said, "In Q2 FY27 TMPV continued to build on its strong momentum in the domestic business, while JLR delivered resilient volumes despite global market-specific challenges and wind-down of previous Jaguar models. However, adverse mix and persistent commodity pressures weighed on margins."
He added that both businesses remained fundamentally strong, with the company's medium-term priorities centred on driving growth through new launches, accelerating cost reductions and improving cash generation.
JLR recovery supports consolidated performance, but exceptional costs weigh on profitability
JLR's revenue increased 20.3% year-on-year to approximately ₹73,455 crore during Q2 FY27, while its profit before tax and exceptional items stood at approximately ₹747 crore, compared with a loss of approximately ₹6,038 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. For the first half of FY27, revenue grew 3.2% to approximately ₹1,48,155 crore.
The improvement in JLR's year-on-year performance reflected the recovery from the previous year's cyber incident. However, adverse market and model mix continued to affect its quarterly profitability.
JLR reported exceptional costs of approximately ₹6,599 crore during the quarter, relating to restructuring activities, including employee separation costs and write-downs of assets and intangible assets under development. Its adjusted EBIT margin stood at 1.1% for the quarter and 2% for the first half.
Against the backdrop of continuing geopolitical risks, market challenges and exceptional costs, JLR revised its full-year guidance. It now expects an adjusted EBIT margin of 2-3% and free cash outflow of approximately ₹15,563 crore.
PB Balaji, Chief Executive Officer, JLR, said, "JLR delivered positive operating profits in the second quarter and first half of the financial year, despite ongoing global challenges. We launched three new products: Range Rover Electric, Range Rover Sport Electric and the show stopping Jaguar Type 01 at a world premiere in New York."
He added that the proposed arrival of Range Rover GT and a new electric Defender product, alongside its growth plans for the US and execution of the Enterprise Missions programme, would support the company's efforts to reduce breakeven volumes to 300,000 units.
The Enterprise Missions programme targets approximately ₹21,165 crore in savings over the next two years through operational simplification, improved efficiency and lower breakeven volumes.
Domestic PV revenue rises 51%, but margins contract 180 bps
On the domestic front, Tata Passenger Vehicles recorded its highest-ever quarterly revenue of ₹20,423 crore, registering a 50.9% year-on-year increase. The business reported 40% growth in volumes, with passenger vehicle sales crossing 200,000 units during the quarter.
Despite the revenue expansion, the domestic business reported an EBITDA margin of 4%, down 180 basis points year-on-year, while EBIT margin stood at negative 0.3%, contracting 50 basis points. The company attributed the margin pressure primarily to adverse commodity and foreign exchange movements.
Profit before tax and exceptional items stood at ₹25 crore, compared with approximately ₹200 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Electric vehicle volumes grew 90% year-on-year, while the business reported a 380-basis-point sequential improvement in EV market share. EV penetration stood at 23% during the quarter, while CNG accounted for 28%, taking the combined penetration of alternative powertrains beyond 50%.
The company also reported positive free cash flow of ₹825 crore for the quarter. Its closing cash balance stood at ₹11,000 crore, against gross debt of ₹3,100 crore, resulting in net cash of ₹7,900 crore.
The quarter also saw the unveiling of Tata.Cars, the company's new consumer-facing global brand identity, alongside the brand promise 'Nothing's Too Far'. The company introduced the all-new Tata Aeris and additional product interventions across its portfolio, including the Curvv Series X, Sierra Legend Series and Sierra #Dark edition. It also extended its Battery-as-a-Service offering across its entire EV portfolio.
Shailesh Chandra, Managing Director and CEO, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, said, "Q2 FY27 was another quarter of strong execution for Tata Motors PV, with record quarterly sales of 200k+ units and industry-beating growth of 40% YoY reflecting robust customer demand across our portfolio. We maintained our leadership in electric mobility, recording industry-beating growth of 90% YoY in EV sales."
On the financial performance, Chandra said the company registered 51% year-on-year revenue growth and its highest-ever quarterly revenue of ₹20,400 crore. He added that commodity cost pressures remained a headwind, prompting the company to respond through calibrated pricing and focused cost actions.
Looking ahead, TMPVL identified global geopolitical developments, luxury vehicle demand trends, the pace of electric vehicle adoption and commodity costs as key factors to monitor. While the domestic business will focus on sustaining industry-beating growth and improving profitability through cost reductions and calibrated pricing, JLR's near-term priorities include building sales momentum through new electric vehicle launches and executing its Enterprise Missions programme.
